entries.text:
In accordance with Late 2026 Sovereign Directives:
1. **Single Public AI Product**: `@aphrody/ai-os` (`packages/ai-os` / `ai-os.exe`) is the sole public AI agent runtime and MCP owner across the entire `C:\src` monorepo.
2. **Triad Orchestration**: `@aphrody/ai-triad` (`packages/ai-triad` / `triad.exe`) orchestrates multi-agent CLI workflows across OpenAI Codex, Google Antigravity (AGY/Gemini), and Anthropic Claude Code.
3. **Domain Agent Plugins**: Domain-specific products (`apps/shenron`, `apps/rosegriffon`) define their own localized plugins (`plugin/` in Shenron) without fragmenting root monorepo toolchains.

entries.title: ARCHGUARD.md
entries.text:
ArchGuard is the automated embodiment of three unified engineering philosophies: ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Linus Torvalds
Systems Taste & Userspace"] --> D["ArchGuard
Engine"] B["Jarred Sumner
Bun Full-Rust Speed"] --> D C["Larry Page
10x Clarity & NHITL"] --> D D --> E["4-Pillar VCS Lock
src.lock.json v2"] ```

entries.title: ARCHGUARD.md
entries.text:
- **Never Break Userspace (`ARCH-007`)**: Windows host directories (`C:\Windows\System32`, `C:\Windows\SysWOW64`) are strictly immutable. All userland binaries live in `C:\Users\aphro\.local\bin` or user winget/Cargo/Bun paths.
- **Good Taste in Data Structures**: Data structures in systems code are flat and cache-friendly without special edge-case branching.
- **Upstream Linux Standards (`ARCH-015`)**: Upstream `MAINTAINERS` file format is validated against disk reality. File patterns `F:` must resolve to actual directories or files. Patch series in `docs/patches/series` follow Quilt / b4 / git-am unified diff standards.

entries.title: ARCHGUARD.md
entries.text:
- **Sub-Millisecond Feedback Loops**: ArchGuard parallelizes file scanning across all CPU cores using Rayon, verifying 2,800+ files in under 5 seconds.
- **Delete Glue & Zero NPM Dependencies (`ARCH-003`, `ARCH-016`)**: First-party packages avoid npm dependency sprawl. Native Bun APIs (`bun:sqlite`, `Bun.serve`, `Bun.build`) and Rust FFI DLLs replace third-party glue. Legacy `binding.gyp` and `postinstall` compilation scripts are banned.

entries.title: ARCHGUARD.md
entries.text:
- **Extreme Surface Simplicity**: High-density capabilities hidden behind a clean CLI surface (`archguard check`, `archguard graph`, `archguard rules`).
- **Cryptographic Audit Digest (`report_blake3`)**: Every audit execution produces an immutable BLAKE3 hash of its findings, providing verifiable reproducibility for CI/CD and AI agent pairs.

---

entries.title: ARCHITECTURE-ROOT.md
entries.text:
1. **Un seul de chaque.** Un workspace Cargo (`crates/*`), un workspace bun (`packages/*`), une toolchain Rust (`rust-toolchain.toml`, une nightly épinglée). Un seul `Cargo.lock`, `bun.lock`, `src.lock.json` (dépôts) et `justfile`. `[workspace.dependencies]` donne une version par crate.
2. **À plat.** `crates/<couche>-<nom>`, `packages/<nom>`, `third_party/<nom>`, sur un seul niveau, sans dossier de catégorie (modèle Chromium). La catégorie devient une métadonnée. Les crates existants changent de dossier mais gardent leur nom de package, pour ne casser aucun dépendant.
3. **Un projet amont = un dossier.** Les forks d'un même réseau GitHub sont réunis :
   - `origin` = fork `aphrody-labs`, `upstream` = projet amont ;
   - un fork tiers qui porte des commits devient un remote supplémentaire du même clone (exemple : `reactos` dans `third_party/LiberNT`), pas une seconde copie ;
   - les patchs vivent dans les forks, épinglés par commit, jamais dans une copie vendorisée.
4. **Rien de régénérable n'est versionné.** `third_party/` (matérialisé depuis `src.lock.json`), `third_party/crates` (`cargo vendor` via `just vendor` : `Cargo.lock` et la source-replace de `.cargo/config.toml` restent versionnés, le build tourne hors ligne), `target/`, `node_modules/`, `var/`.
5. **Identité unique.** `identity.toml` à la racine contient : nom du dépôt, CLI, scope npm, préfixe des crates, domaine, remotes git et Lore.
   - `ay identity apply` réécrit les `name`, `[[bin]]`, `package.json#name` et remotes ;
   - `ay identity check` sert de garde de CI ;
   - le code n'écrit aucun nom de produit en dur : il utilise `env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME")`, `CARGO_BIN_NAME` ou une crate `identity` générée par build.rs ;
   - renommer tient en une PR : identity.toml, puis `apply`, puis `just ci`.
6. **Aucun chemin absolu, lien ni jonction.**
   - Les chemins sont relatifs à la racine, détectée par `Cargo.toml` ou `.lore`.
   - Sinon ils viennent des variables d'environnement (`XDG_*`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, `SystemRoot`).
7. **Multiplateforme.** Chaque binaire compile et teste sur windows-msvc et linux-gnu. `just` appelle des binaires Rust ou bun : aucun `.sh` ni `.ps1` requis. Les recettes propres à un OS sont marquées `[windows]` ou `[unix]`.
8. **Pas de régression.** Après chaque phase, les nombres de tests doivent être égaux ou supérieurs à la base. Une phase qui casse est annulée. Exécution sur prd ou fr2 uniquement : consigne du propriétaire, aucune compilation sur le PC ni sur fr1.

entries.title: ARCHITECTURE-ROOT.md
entries.text:
- 320 dépôts → 309 projets amont : 277 déplacements, 10 doublons supprimés, 1 dossier vide retiré (320 − 10 − 1 = 309). Limite : la comparaison GitHub ne porte que sur la branche par défaut ; vérifier aussi branches, tags et amonts hors GitHub avant suppression.
  - Doublons détectés par l'API GitHub, en suivant le réseau de forks et le nombre de commits d'avance (« ahead »). Exemples : `cachyos/WSL` (fork de microsoft/WSL, 0 commit d'avance, 67 de retard) et `build/wild` (aphrody-dev, 0 d'avance).
  - Autres opérations : 3 jonctions retirées, 1 dossier vide, 2 fichiers isolés déplacés vers `var/`, 26 références suivies réécrites.
- Nommage. Le nom est le dernier segment du chemin actuel, sans le préfixe `owner_`. Un nom générique garde son propriétaire (`lightpanda-io-browser`, `modelcontextprotocol-rust-sdk`). Les exceptions sont listées et justifiées dans le script.
- Sûreté. Le plan est refusé dans quatre cas : collision, dossier non verrouillé, travail local dans un doublon, fork divergent.
- Application. Le déplacement passe par un transit `third_party/.flatten`. Les dossiers de catégorie sont retirés par `rmdir`, qui échoue s'ils ne sont pas vides.
- Calendrier : après le merge labs, puis `ay lock --lock-only`.

entries.title: AY_MIGRATION.md
entries.text:
1. **Production runs on fr1, not usa.** Of the 106 web hostnames in aphrody.com, aphrody.app and
   rosegriffon.fr, 21 aphrody.app A records and 4 aphrody.com A records point to fr1. The 38
   aphrody.com CNAMEs follow the apex, which is an A record to fr1 (DNS-only). `api.aphrody.com`
   and `vps.aphrody.com` also carry fr1's IPv6 address. fr1 nginx serves aphrody.com and its
   subdomains from `aphrody-web` (:3000), `aphrody-app` (:3010), `aphrody-site` (:8083), store,
   downloads, chat and the fonts proxy, out of a `/opt/aphrody/monorepo` checkout. Separately,
   `infra/internal/providers/vps.go` still rejects every non-Google workload on usa. That
   contradicts `deploy.toml` (`allow_non_google_workloads = true`) and the owner decision, so
   `ay deploy up` to usa fails today.
2. **70 of the 106 hostnames are already down with Cloudflare 526** (invalid origin certificate).
   The affected set: `aphrody.app`, `www.aphrody.app`, all 15 `app-*.aphrody.app`, the 15 `*craft`
   names, and 30 aphrody.com subdomains (search, docs, drive, mail, maps, ...). They are proxied,
   but no origin vhost on fr1 has a valid certificate for them. `omar.aphrody.com` and
   `desktop.aphrody.app` return 502. `rosegriffon.fr` returned 502 at 07:12 while its usa compose
   stack restarted and 200 at 08:20. On fr1, `rg-website` is `failed` and `rg-core` is `inactive`.
   DNS for rosegriffon already points to usa, so the fr1 rosegriffon vhosts are dead configuration.
3. **The `aphrody infra`, `yolo`, `backend` and `ovh` commands already exist** in a Rust multicall
   binary, `aphrody 1.0.0-canary`. It is 335 MB in `/usr/local/bin/aphrody` on fr1 and 331 MB in
   `~/.local/bin/aphrody` on fr2. It has 40 commands and also answers to the former binary names
   (`infra, ovh, yolo, kernel, host-service, ssh, wsl, backend, ...`). It was built from
   `aphrody-labs/bun-os`, **which no longer exists on GitHub (404)**. The 34,629-commit history
   survives only in host clones: fr1 `~/src/bun-os`, usa `/root/src/bun-os` (3.2 GB) and
   `/srv/yolo-fleet/wii-os`, and fr2 `~/src/bun-os`. The code survives byte-identical in
   `yolo-rs/yolo-backend` on GitHub, and without history in `C:\src\var\legacy\bunos`
   (gitignored). Crate sizes, in lines:

   | Crate                    | Lines  |
   | ------------------------ | ------ |
   | `aphrody-infra`          | 20,358 |
   | `aphrody-ovh`            | 6,473  |
   | `aphrody-remote-desktop` | 4,816  |
   | `aphrody-ssh`            | 4,521  |
   | `aphrody-inventory`      | 3,394  |
   | `aphrody-jobs`           | 3,126  |
   | `aphrody-gateway`        | 2,722  |
   | `aphrody-yolo`           | 1,979  |
   | `aphrody-wireguard`      | 1,878  |
   | `aphrody-secrets`        | 1,174  |
   | `aphrody-backend`        | 958    |
   | `aphrody-vpn`            | 497    |

4. **All three nodes run the same yolo stack.** On usa, fr1 and fr2 the md5 hashes of
   `/opt/yolo-vps/agent/*.ts`, `/opt/yolo-git-sync/auto-deploy.ts` and
   `/opt/yolo-cf/bin/yolo-cf-gateway` match. Each node runs `yolo-vps-agent`, `yolo-auto-deploy`,
   `yolo-ram-cache`, `yolo-cf-{garage,rqlite,workerd,gateway}`, the `yolo-repo-purge` timer,
   `aphrody-ai`, `hermes-agent` and `opencode-agent`. That is 12 duplicated units on 3 nodes, with
   about 0.9 GB of `/opt/yolo-cf` binaries per node.
5. **The yolo-cf "self-hosted Cloudflare" has no clients.** The only established connections to
   ports 17080-17903 were garage RPC between the three peers. No nginx route on any node points at
   it. It duplicates real Cloudflare, which is now reachable with a verified API token. rqlite runs
   with `-bootstrap-expect=3`, so retire it on all three nodes at once.
6. **`yolo-ram-cache` exists to consume RAM.** Its own header says it targets "78% productive RAM
   utilization". It fallocates `/dev/shm` slabs of 12 GB on fr1, 8 GB on usa and 5 GB on fr2.
   Measured cgroup memory: 27.9 GB on fr1 (45 GiB host, load average 52 on 12 vCPU), 4.9 GB on usa
   and 4.5 G

entries.title: AY_ON_BUN.md
entries.text:
Dependency walk over normal (non-dev, non-build) workspace edges; proc-macro crates are compile-time
only and do not link anything.

- **70 of 136 crates are free of both JSC and the JS/TS engine**: alloc, analytics, archive,
  base64, boringssl(+sys), brotli(+sys), cares_sys, clap, collections, core, crash_handler, csrf,
  dispatch, dns, dotenv, errno, exe_format, glob, hash, highway, histogram, http_types, io,
  libdeflate_sys, libuv_sys, lsquic_sys, md, mimalloc_sys, node_path, output, paths, perf,
  picohttp, platform, png, ptr, s3_signing, safety, semver, sha_hmac, shell_parser, spawn_sys, sql,
  sys, tar, tcc_sys, text_diff, threading, url, uws_sys, valkey, watcher, which, windows_sys,
  wyhash, zlib(+sys), zstd, and others.
- **Also free of JSC and of the JS/TS engine**: `bun_http`, `bun_ini`, `bun_event_loop`,
  `bun_spawn`, `bun_patch`, `bun_uws`, `bun_css`, `bun_sourcemap`, `bun_format`, `bun_parsers`,
  `bun_options_types`, `bun_install_types`. They depend on `bun_jsc_macros`, which is a proc-macro
  with no dependencies (no JSC linked), and on `bun_ast`, a plain Rust AST used for JSON/TOML/YAML
  (deps: alloc, collections, core, dispatch, paths, perf, ptr, sys, wyhash).
- **Only `bun_executable` reaches JSC** (`bun_executable > bun_runtime > bun_sys_jsc`). ay never
  links it.
- **Exactly two edges pull the JS/TS engine into otherwise reusable crates**:
  1. `bun_install > bun_transpiler`: used only in `RunCommand::configure_env_for_run`
     (`src/install/lib.rs:796`) to build a resolver and env loader for lifecycle scripts, plus the
     `Error::Transpiler` variant (`src/install/error.rs:231`).
  2. `bun_resolver > bun_resolve_builtins`: a table of Node builtin aliases
     (`src/resolver/resolver.rs:55`, `:1439`).
  Through `bun_resolver` these edges also reach `bun_bunfig`, `bun_router` and
  `bun_standalone_graph`.
- **Build prerequisites**: the fork pins `nightly-2026-09-15` (`rust-toolchain.toml`) and needs its
  vendored C deps checked out (`cargo check` fails with `no matching package named lol_html`
  until `vendor/lolhtml` exists; fetched by `scripts/vendor-checkout.ts` /
  `scripts/prefetch-deps.ts`). Release builds rely on `scripts/build/rust.ts` for cross-language
  ThinLTO.

entries.title: AY_ON_BUN.md
entries.text:
1. **Fork checkout and baseline.** Run the fork's vendor checkout, then `cargo check` on the 70
   free crates plus the 12 listed above. Proof: clean check log committed to the fork's PR notes.
2. **Cut the two edges** in `aphrody-dev/bun` behind the default-on features. Proof: `cargo tree`
   as above; Bun's own `bun bd` and its install/resolver test suites still pass.
3. **First routes**: `ay sh`, `ay x`, `ay fetch`, `ay tar`/`zstd`, `ay glob`, `ay semver`
   (no install yet). Proof: `cargo test -p aphrody` routing tests; `ay sh` runs the justfile's
   cross-platform recipes on Windows and Linux (musl via `cargo zigbuild`).
4. **`ay install`** on `bun_install` with `scripts-runtime` off. Proof: on `packages/env-kit` and
   one app, `ay install --frozen-lockfile` produces the same `node_modules` tree and `bun.lock` as
   `bun install --frozen-lockfile` (diff of `bun pm ls --all`).
5. **Size and speed budget**: record `ay` binary size and cold-start time before and after; target
   no regression on `ay --version` start time. Proof: `hyperfine` numbers in this file.
6. **Retire duplicates** in ay that the fork crates replace (ad hoc HTTP, tar, glob code in
   `crates/depot-*`, `crates/up`). Proof: `rg` shows no remaining users; all suites green.

crate. Final is this repository's config with those two environment variables

| No-op             | 0.68 s (0.96) | 0.72 s (0.85) | noise |

Clean build critical path (cargo `--timings`, 60 s run):
`ash` build script -> `ash` (10 s, frontend bound) -> `gpu-allocator` ->
`wgpu-hal` (7 s) -> `wgpu-core` (10 s) -> `sovereign-corelib` -> `rust-stack`
(11.6 s, 9 s of codegen at `opt-level = 1`) -> `rust-stack` binary.
Other heavy units off the critical path: `windows` 0.62 (13.6 s),
`lightningcss` (13.5 s), `naga` (13.5 s), `gix` (8.7 s), `iced-x86`, `rustls`.

Core edit (3.7 s in that run): 0.9 s of cargo start-up and fingerprinting before
the first rustc, depot-core 0.9 s, its three dependents 0.7 s in parallel, then
the four depot-cli binaries and the depot-ffi cdylib, 1.4 to 1.8 s each, mostly
link. The no-op floor (0.7 s) is cargo stat-ing 636 units on NTFS with Defender
real-time scanning.

entries.title: BUILD_SPEED.md
entries.text:
Reproduced with `cargo build -p gamescope-web-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
web-sys passes one `--check-cfg cfg(feature, values(...))` argument listing
every web-sys feature, which pushes the rustc command line past the 32 767
character limit of `CreateProcess`. Cargo falls back to an `@argfile`, but
sccache expands it and spawns rustc with the full line, which fails. The same
build passes without the wrapper, in dev and release. A shorter build dir would
not help, since the long argument is not a path.

entries.title: BUN_1_4_4_CANONICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
1. **Zero unnecessary `dependencies` in packages**: All first-party workspace packages (`packages/*`) maintain 0 external npm dependencies when native Bun v1.4.4 APIs suffice.
2. **Canonical `tsconfig.json`**: Every workspace package defines `"allowImportingTsExtensions": true`, `"noEmit": true`, and `"types": ["bun"]`.
3. **Sacred Host Userspace**: Zero binaries placed in `C:\Windows\System32`. Sovereign binaries compile to `C:\Users\aphro\.local\bin` via `bun build --compile`.
4. **Single AI Ownership**: `@aphrody/ai-os` (`packages/ai-os`) is the sole public AI product and MCP server (`ai-os.exe mcp-stdio`). All other surfaces (`apps/*`, `crates/*`) are generalist platforms without AI slop.

entries.title: BUN_1_4_4_SHENRON_NATIVE_CONSOLIDATION.md
entries.text:
Historically, `apps/shenron` and `apps/rosegriffon` accumulated fragile third-party and transitional wrapper dependencies (`postgres`, `pg`, `aws4fetch`, `sharp`, `modern-gif`, `@paralleldrive/cuid2`, `undici`, `undici-types`, `axios`, `pino`, `@aphrody/sql`, `@aphrody/http`, `@aphrody/paths`, `@aphrody/bun-video`, `@aphrody/bun-types`, `turbo`, `@changesets/cli`, and `bunx` script runners). Those packages introduce:

1. **Private Registry & Tarball Fragility**: Scoped `@aphrody/*` shims (`@aphrody/sql`, `@aphrody/http`, `@aphrody/paths`, `@aphrody/bun-video`, `@aphrody/bun-types`) and `bunx` on-demand CLI downloads fail in air-gapped builds, Docker multi-stage layers, or fresh VPS checkouts without registry tokens.
2. **Native Node-API (`node-gyp` / `.node`) ABI Drift**: `sharp` (`libvips` C++ prebuilds) and Node native addons complicate `bun build --compile --bytecode` single-binary distribution across Windows 11 (`x64`) and Linux (`x64`).
3. **Redundant JavaScript Glue**: `postgres`, `aws4fetch`, `undici`, `axios`, `pino`, `@paralleldrive/cuid2`, `turbo`, and `@changesets/cli` re-implement in userland JavaScript what Bun v1.4.4 already executes natively in Rust/Zig/C++ inside the runtime binary.

Empirical measurements from [`packages/chromium-bun/REPORT.md`](file:///C:/src/packages/chromium-bun/REPORT.md) confirm the vertical speedup of native Bun v1.4.4 primitives on our reference hardware (Intel Core i7-13700F 16C/24T, 32 GB DDR5-5800, Windows 11 NT):

| Workload | Native Bun v1.4.4 Primitive | Measured Performance | Legacy Baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TypeScript Typechecking | `bun check` (multi-core Rust TS7) | **21–37 ms** per package | `tsc --noEmit` (~1,200–4,500 ms) |
| Bundling + Minification | `Bun.build` (native Rust bundler) | **7.73 ms** | Rollup / Terser / Webpack (500+ ms) |
| TypeScript Transpilation | `Bun.Transpiler` | **100 files in 7.86 ms** (12,722 files/s) | `tsup` / `esbuild` spawn |
| SQLite Batch Writes | `bun:sqlite` (WAL transaction) | **10,000 rows in 4.30 ms** (2.32M rows/s) | `better-sqlite3` / JSON disk cache |
| Non-Crypto Hashing | `Bun.hash` (`wyhash` / `crc32` / `xxHash3`) | **25.73 GB/s** (`crc32` 15.86 GB/s) | JS `cuid2` / `crypto.createHash` |
| Compression | `Bun.zstdCompressSync` | **2,202 MB/s** (3.7x faster than gzip) | npm `fzstd` / `zlib` |
| Subprocess / CLI Startup | `bun` / AOT `--compile --bytecode` | **11.10 ms** cold start (8.16x faster than `pwsh`) | `bunx` / `npx` / `turbo` |

---

entries.title: BUN_1_4_4_SHENRON_NATIVE_CONSOLIDATION.md
entries.text:
Zero-dependency Bun bundler/runtime plugin suite providing four virtual/loader integrations:

1. **`justPlugin` ([`just-plugin.ts`](file:///C:/src/packages/bun-plugins/just-plugin.ts))**: Parses `justfile` recipes directly in Bun (`loader: "js"`) so TypeScript tools can `import { recipes, runRecipe } from "./justfile"` without shelling out to inspect task graphs.
2. **`TurboCache` & `turboCachePlugin` ([`turbo-cache-plugin.ts`](file:///C:/src/packages/bun-plugins/turbo-cache-plugin.ts))**: Content-addressed task memoization (`import { defaultCache } from "turbo:cache"`) powered by `new Bun.CryptoHasher("blake2s256")` over command strings, sorted env keys, and input file digests — replacing `turbo` without external dependencies.
3. **`vcsMetaPlugin` ([`vcs-meta-plugin.ts`](file:///C:/src/packages/bun-plugins/vcs-meta-plugin.ts))**: Virtual module `vcs:meta` exposing Jujutsu (`jj` change ID) and Git (`commitHash`, `shortHash`, `branch`, `dirty`, `timestamp`) metadata at runtime or `--compile` bundle time.
4. **`decidePlugin` ([`decide-plugin.ts`](file:///C:/src/packages/bun-plugins/decide-plugin.ts))**: Compile-time `.decide` state-machine compiler bridging `sov_core.dll` via `bun:ffi` (`dlopen`, `CString`, `ptr`) with zero runtime overhead.
5. **`bun-native.d.ts` ([`bun-native.d.ts`](file:///C:/src/packages/bun-plugins/bun-native.d.ts))**: Shared zero-dependency ambient type header enabling `"dependencies": {}, "devDependencies": {}` across `packages/bun-plugins`, `packages/brain`, `packages/chromium-bun`, `packages/pi-opencode`, and `infra/ffi-bridge`.

entries.title: BUN_1_4_4_SHENRON_NATIVE_CONSOLIDATION.md
entries.text:
Zero-dependency Chromium-vs-Bun Web Standards recon & preload engine (`bpt`), elevating Bun v1.4.4 to 100% parity across 10 browser/edge domains without npm packages:

- **Prioritized Task Scheduling**: `globalThis.scheduler.postTask()` & `scheduler.yield()` with `TaskController` priorities (`user-blocking`, `user-visible`, `background`).
- **W3C Web Locks API**: `navigator.locks.request()` supporting `exclusive` and `shared` modes, `ifAvailable`, and `AbortSignal`.
- **W3C CacheStorage Backed by `bun:sqlite`**: `globalThis.caches.open()` persisted in SQLite (`CREATE TABLE cache_entries`), replacing Redis/in-memory response caches for edge SSR.
- **Extended `CompressionStream`**: Adds `"br"` (Brotli via `node:zlib` native binding) alongside Bun's native `"gzip"`, `"deflate"`, `"deflate-raw"`, and `"zstd"`.
- **W3C Trusted Types & RFC 8484 DoH**: `trustedTypes.createPolicy()` and DNS-over-HTTPS Type 65 (`HTTPS` / `SVCB` ALPN HTTP/3 h3 discovery).

entries.title: CHROMIUM-FACTORY.md
entries.text:
1. **Exécution + cache distants REAPI en Rust : NativeLink** (TraceMachina/nativelink, Rust, push 2026-11-12). siso parle REAPI nativement : `-reapi_address`, `-reapi_instance`, `-reapi_insecure`, `-re_cache_enable_write` (vérifié `siso ninja -help` sur fr1). Scheduler + CAS sur fr1, workers fr1 + prd + fr2 (26 cœurs au lieu de 12) via le mesh, sans TLS (réseau privé). Le cache d'actions rend les rebuilds Stable→Beta→Dev et les re-runs quasi gratuits pour tout ce qui n'a pas changé (third_party).
2. **siso `-local_cache_enable`** : gratuit, immédiat, utile en attendant 1.
3. **Sync en Rust** : `ay gclient sync --apply --populate-cache -j 24` (gitoxide, cache git partagé par alternates) à la place de `gclient sync` Python ; runhooks via `ay gclient runhooks` + `ay vpy`. Sync incrémental entre canaux = fetch des seuls objets manquants.
4. **Artefacts** : sortie publiée dans depot-cas (FastCDC) + R2 au lieu de zstd -19 entier : seuls les fragments changés remontent.
5. **Builds par composant** : v8 (d8, wasm), dawn (tint, dawn_end2end), skia (dm, viewer) en cibles GN séparées dans le même out/ partagé → profitent du même cache REAPI.

entries.title: CHROMIUM-FACTORY.md
entries.text:
- Cause racine du « Permission denied (os error 13) » : systemd 262 (prd, Arch) monte le StateDirectory DynamicUser (`/var/lib/private`) en `noexec,nosuid,idmapped` dans le namespace du service. Le bit exec est bien conservé (NativeLink garde les exécutables en 0555 dans `cas.exec/`), c'est le montage qui bloque `execve`. Reproduit avec `systemd-run -p DynamicUser=yes -p StateDirectory=nativelink …` : clang → EACCES ; avec `-p ExecPaths=/var/lib/private/nativelink` → OK. fr2 (systemd 261) n'était pas concerné.
- Correctif (`infra/chromium-factory/nativelink/deploy.sh`) : `ExecPaths=/var/lib/private/nativelink` sur l'unité worker ; DynamicUser, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=read-only, NoNewPrivileges conservés (pas de root).
- Redéployé : server fr1, workers prd (80 GB de cache) et fr2 (20 GB) actifs.
- Test (fr1, `nice -n 19`, `out/re-test`, use_remoteexec=true) : `sys_info.o` + `file_path.o` → remote:1 (exécuté sur fr2, exit 0), cache:1, 0 erreur ; second run après suppression des .o (`rand_util.o`, `sys_info.o`, `file_path.o`) → cache:3 remote:0, 0 erreur reapi.
- Restent à faire : worker fr1 (F0 `chromium-factory-build` relancé et actif au moment du test) ; rebuild complet depuis un out/ vide pour mesurer la durée froide et le taux AC.

entries.text:
Remplace les « gains attendus » estimés. Code : `tools/build-model/` (Rust ; `cargo test` vérifie DP, bornes et simulation sur DAG synthétiques à réponse connue et sur 300 DAG aléatoires). Reproduction : `tools/build-model/run.sh`. Sortie brute : `tools/build-model/results/2026-11-12-report.txt`. Règles : `docs/SCIENTIFIC-RIGOR.md`.

Entrées (mesurées)

| Entrée | Source | Valeur |
|---|---|---|
| DAG | `siso query graph` (fr1, graphe actuel, `dawn_enable_vulkan_validation_layers=false`), fermeture arrière de `headless_shell`, arêtes = inputs + implicit + order-only | 62 034 nœuds dont 21 819 phony (poids 0) ; 40 215 actions |
| Poids mesurés | `run_nanos` de siso_metrics, run 1 + run 2 (run 2 prioritaire) | 31 124 actions |
| Normalisation | processus en vol mesurés (exec_start/exec_nanos) : jusqu'à 25 pendant les 50 premières minutes du run 1, 12 ensuite ; poids × min(1, 12/c) au milieu de l'action (partage de processeur) | 10 011 / 29 714 steps corrigés ; 140 339 → 127 095 slot·s |
| Imputation | actions non exécutées : tirage dans la distribution empirique classe (cxx/cc/link/alink/rust/action/copy) × répertoire 2 niveaux, repli 1 niveau puis classe, n ≥ 5 | 9 091 actions = 22,6 % des actions, 29,2 % de T1 |
| Efficacité CPU η | rusage enfant (utime+stime) réparti par minute, run 1, n = 176 min | 8,02 cœurs effectifs [IC 95 % bootstrap par blocs de 15 min : 7,54–8,54], médiane 8,44, IQR 7,80–8,81 ; η = 0,669 [0,629–0,712] ; ρ = ΣCPU/Σslot = 0,605 |
| Vitesse par cœur | boucle awk 2·10⁷ itérations, n = 10 par hôte, médiane | fr1 1 549 ms, prd 1 438 ms (load 11–38 pendant la mesure), fr2 1 893 ms → s = 1,077 (prd), 0,819 (fr2) |
| Action distante | re-test, 1 action sur fr2 | exec 1,34 s contre 5,23 s en local sous charge ; input_fetch à froid 11,07 s (n = 1 : insuffisant pour un facteur, sert de borne) |
| Réseau fr1 → prd (WireGuard) | 5 × 32 MiB via ssh, 1 × 105 MB | 28,9–154,7 Mbit/s, médiane 100,6 ; RTT 8,4 ms (n = 20) |
| Sorties | `*.o` dans out/ | 25 362 fichiers, 2,41 GB, moyenne 94,9 kB → overhead chaud o = 2 RTT + 94,9 kB / 100,6 Mbit/s ≈ 0,025 s |
| Cache AC | re-test, 2e run | 3/3 hits, Wilson 95 % [0,438 ; 1] ; coût d'un hit 0,178 s (n = 3) |

Formules

- T1 = Σ w(v) ; T∞ = plus long chemin pondéré (DP en ordre topologique : f(v) = w(v) + max f(u), u → v).
- p slots identiques, ordonnancement glouton (Graham/Brent) : max(T1/p, T∞) ≤ Tp ≤ T1/p + T∞.
- Slots hétérogènes de vitesses s_i et overhead o_i (durée w/s_i + o_i) : Tp ≥ max(T1/Σs_i, T∞/s_max) ; Tp ≤ Σd/p + CP(d) avec d = w/s_min + o_max (argument de Graham en unités d ; vérifié par les tests sur DAG aléatoires).
- Unité : slot·s de fr1 à 12 processus en vol. Pool REAPI : fr1 14 slots (4 local + 10 worker sur 12 cœurs → s = 12/14), prd 4, fr2 3. Trois jeux : `mid` s = ratio du micro-bench, o = 0,025 s ; `opt` s = ratio / 0,668 (action distante sans contention : durée = CPU ; 0,668 = ΣCPU/Σw normalisé) ; `coldcas` s = ratio, o = 11,07 s (CAS froid à chaque action, pire cas).
- Cache : w_h = h·c_hit + (1−h)·w ; link final toujours exécuté (hypothèse [NV] : link local, hors cache).
- Incertitude : bootstrap B = 1 000 sur les durées imputées (graine 20261112), percentiles 2,5/50/97,5. Les durées mesurées sont fixes : le bruit d'un run à l'autre n'est pas capturé.

Résultats (bornes = [basse ; haute], médianes bootstrap ; « sim » = glouton chemin critique simulé, médiane [IC 95 %])

| Build froid complet (40 215 actions) | 53,93 h [53,49–54,37] | 479 s [468–637] | [4,49 ; 4,63] h, sim 4,50 h [4,46–4,54] | [2,87 ; 3,31] h, sim 2,88 h [2,86–2,91] | [2,44 ; 3,17] h, sim 2,45 h | [2,87 ; 9,38] h, sim 3,63 h |

entries.title: CHROMIUM-FACTORY.md
entries.text:
Crate `crates/factory` (package `aphrody-factory`, lib + bin mince ; `tool_main(&[OsString]) -> i32` pour `ay factory`). Les canaux sont lus via `aphrody_conformance::channels::parse_toml`, sans second parseur. Pour `sync`, gclient reste le défaut ; `ay gclient sync --apply --populate-cache --cipd` est derrière `sync_with_ay` tant que F3 ne l'a pas validé. `ay gclient runhooks` et `revinfo` sont appelés directement (F3 : 0 diff).

| Commande | Effet |
|---|---|
| `doctor` | disque src ≥ 40 GiB et CAS ≥ 160 GiB, MemAvailable ≥ 16 GiB, pas de build concurrent, outils (siso, gn, ay, gclient, rclone), NativeLink :50051/:50061, workers connectés (`ss` sur :50061), toolchain conforme à `third_party/toolchain-<milestone>.toml` (cr_build_revision, VERSION rust, `clang --version`, `rustc --version`, stamps blake3), checkout sur le tag du canal |
| `sync [--refresh-channels]` | fetch au premier passage, tag du canal, `checkout_pgo_profiles`, gclient sync, install-build-deps une seule fois, `ay gclient runhooks`, `revinfo-<ver>.txt` |
| `gen` | `out/labs_agent/args.gn` = args + bloc généré (`use_siso`, `use_remoteexec`), `gn gen` |
| `build [--offline] [--skip-doctor]` | doctor (bloquant en FAIL), siso avec les flags REAPI, résumé de siso_metrics.json dans l'état |
| `publish` | tar `zstd -T0 -19` + manifeste JSON → `r2-chromium:aphrody-chromium/labs_agent/<ver>/linux-x64.{tar.zst,json}` |
| `all` | sync → gen → build → publish ; chaque étape a une clé (version + hash des entrées) dans `/srv/chromium/factory-state.json` et n'est pas rejouée sans `--force` |
| `status` | canal, état, out/, dernier résumé de build |
| `toolchain install` / `check` `[--platform]` | rclone depuis R2, vérification taille + sha256 + blake3, extraction dans `third_party/llvm-build/Release+Asserts` et `third_party/rust-toolchain`, stamp `.aphrody-toolchain` |

Déploiement sur fr1 (pas fait : rien n'est activé tant que le build est arrêté)

1. prd : `cargo build --release -p aphrody-factory`, copie vers `fr1:/srv/chromium/factory/bin/aphrody-factory` (même glibc 2.44).
2. fr1 : `infra/chromium-factory/{factory.toml,args/,systemd/}` et `third_party/{chrome-channels.toml,toolchain-157.toml}` dans `/srv/chromium/factory/`.
3. Redéployer le server (bytestream) : `deploy.sh server`. Worker fr1 : `deploy.sh worker 10.200.77.1 100000000000 10`. Workers prd et fr2 : `deploy.sh worker 10.200.77.1 <cache> 4` ou `3`.
4. `aphrody-factory doctor`, puis `aphrody-factory all`, ou l'unité `chromium-factory.service` avec son timer.

Validation : `cargo test -p aphrody-factory` sur prd, 21 tests OK, clippy sans avertissement sur la crate. `doctor` lancé en lecture seule sur fr1 : disque, RAM, outils, NativeLink et toolchain 157 OK ; prd et fr2 connectés ; fr1 sans worker (attendu).

entries.title: CONFORMANCE.md
entries.text:
- Each pin lives in `conformance/upstreams.toml` (`repo`, `commit`, `license`, `pinned_on`; suites list their `paths`), and the table above is generated from it. Branch names are never used as refs.
- Pins are bumped only by a dedicated change (`aphrody x conformance bump <suite>`) that runs the suite before and after and records the delta in the change description. Bumps happen monthly, or when the supported Next.js or Tailwind line moves.
- Each suite has an expected-failures file, `conformance/expected/<suite>.txt`, with one test id and one reason per line. A test that moves from pass to fail fails CI. A test that starts passing must be removed from the file in the same change.
- Denominators are frozen per pin, so pass rates are comparable across commits of this repo. The denominator changes only with a pin bump.

entries.title: CONSOLIDATION_PLAN.md
entries.text:
- Clean Rust: flat workspace, no crates nested inside crates, no dead code, Cargo best practices.
- Published crates.io dependencies instead of vendored copies; minimal vendoring.
- Duplicated projects merged; thin TypeScript packages turned into scripts, useful ones kept.
- One full-Rust, LTO + AOT CLI that manages the whole repo: VCS (git, gix, depot_tools, repo), code ingest and graphs (gitingest, graphify, tree-sitter), architecture gate, distro tooling (CachyOS, Omarchy, kernel), Bun and Chromium tooling, deploy.
- A real build factory: cross-compilation for native Rust, C++ (Chromium), Bun, and WASM apps, with one FFI story.
- aphrody.app: a full-Rust monorepo product that builds, deploys, monitors and links native Rust, WASM and C++ apps, with a correct FFI layer, LTO/AOT, and cross-compilation in mind.

entries.title: DEPOT_ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
Modern large-scale development environments—spanning multi-gigabyte codebases such as Chromium, Unreal Engine 6, AOSP, and LLM-driven autonomous agent swarms—face two existential bottlenecks in version control:
1. **Repository Weight & Object Bloat**: Full Git clones download gigabytes of historical object trees and binary blobs, choking disk I/O, network bandwidth, and filesystem monitoring.
2. **LLM Context Window Inefficiency**: Large Language Models (LLMs) cannot ingest raw 100,000-file repositories without deterministic filtering, smart token budgeting, structural AST summarization, and noise elimination (lockfiles, build artifacts, compiled binaries).

The **Depot** ecosystem (`C:\src\crates\depot`) unifies Google's **`depot_tools`**, **Unreal Engine's CDN binary artifact architecture**, **Microsoft Git Scalar**, **Jujutsu (`jj`)**, **`gitoxide` (`gix`)**, **`gitingest`**, and **`graphify`** into a high-performance, native Rust 2024 monorepo with `justfile` automation.

---

entries.title: DEPOT_ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
Unlike Git submodules which record fixed Git tree hashes directly in the parent tree object, Google's `gclient` uses Python-evaluated declarative manifest files named `DEPS`:
- **`solutions`**: Defined in the root `.gclient` file, identifying top-level repositories and checkout modes.
- **`vars` and `deps`**: Dynamic mapping of paths to Git URLs pinned to specific commit hashes or CIPD packages.
- **Conditional Dependencies (`deps_os`)**: Platform-specific sub-repositories (e.g., checkout Windows SDK tools only on Windows).

entries.title: DEPOT_ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
To avoid downloading tens of gigabytes across multiple local checkouts or clean CI builds:
- `depot_tools` maintains a centralized bare Git mirror in `LOCALAPPDATA/depot_tools/git_cache` (e.g. `chromium.googlesource.com-chromium-src`).
- New working checkouts are initialized with `git clone --shared` or `git clone --reference <cache_dir>`.
- The checkout's `.git/objects/info/alternates` file points directly to the shared local mirror. Disk consumption per checkout is reduced from 40+ GB down to the working tree files alone.

entries.title: DEPOT_ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
Google completely separates binary toolchains from Git history using CIPD (`cipd.exe`):
- Compilers (Clang/LLVM), Python runtimes, Node/Bun runtimes, GN binaries, and test fixtures are packaged as content-addressed zip archives on Google Cloud Storage.
- `DEPS` pins CIPD packages by SHA-256 instance IDs (e.g. `package: infra/tools/cipd/windows-amd64@<hash>`).
- CIPD extracts binaries directly into designated directories without committing a single byte to Git history.

entries.title: DEPOT_ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
Chromium provides `gclient-new-workdir.py` to clone workdirs quickly. However, line 26 of Google's script contains:
```python
if sys.platform == "win32":
    print("ERROR: This script cannot run on Windows because it uses symlinks.")
    sys.exit(1)
```
Depot solves this natively: `depot worktree` replaces brittle Unix symlinks with native `git worktree` and directory junction management, functioning 100% reliably on Windows NT NTFS.

---

entries.title: DEPOT_ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
Epic Games prevents Git object bloat through a proprietary tool:
- The Git repository contains only source code, shaders, build rules, and metadata.
- Precompiled third-party libraries (DirectX, Vulkan, PhysX, Chaos, consoles SDKs) are tracked in `.ue4dependencies` / `Commit.gitdeps.xml`.
- When running `Setup.bat`, `GitDependencies.exe` reads the XML/manifest, computes SHA-1/SHA-256 hashes of local files, and downloads compressed chunks (`.pack`) from an Amazon CloudFront CDN.
- Git history stays lean (under 2 GB of text source code), while binary SDKs are fetched on demand.

entries.title: DEPOT_ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
To handle 100,000+ files efficiently on Windows, Microsoft developed GVFS, now standardized into upstream Git as **Git Scalar**:
- **Blobless Clone (`--filter=blob:none`)**: Downloads commit trees and metadata instantly; file contents (blobs) are downloaded lazily on checkout or read.
- **Filesystem Monitor (`core.fsmonitor=true`)**: Hooks into the Windows NTFS Change Journal (`USN Journal`) or daemon to track file modifications without calling `stat()` on 200,000 files.
- **Many-Files Index Optimization (`feature.manyFiles=true`)**: Enables `index.version 4` with prefix compression and untracked cache (`core.untrackedCache=true`).
- **Commit Graph & Multi-Pack-Index**: Background maintenance (`scalar register`, `git commit-graph write --reachable --changed-paths`, `git multi-pack-index write`) keeps commit traversals instantaneous.

---

entries.title: DEPOT_ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
| Metric / Capability | Git C (Default) | Google `depot_tools` | Epic Games UE | `gitoxide` (`gix`) | Jujutsu (`jj`) | **Depot (`depot`)** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Language** | C / Shell / Perl | Python / Batch | C# / C++ | Pure Rust 2024 | Pure Rust 2024 | **Pure Rust 2024** |
| **Windows Support** | Good (Git for Win) | Partial (`workdir` fails) | Native | Native | Native | **100% Native NTFS** |
| **Minimal Git Weight** | Manual flags | Mirror + alternates | GitDependencies | Native streaming | Git-backed | **Scalar + Blobless Auto** |
| **Binary Artifacts** | Git LFS (heavy) | CIPD packages | CDN `.ue4dependencies`| Custom | External | **Blake3 Manifest TOML** |
| **LLM Ingest Engine** | None | None | None | None | None | **Native Ingest (100x speed)**|
| **AST Knowledge Graph**| None | None | None | None | None | **Native Graphify AST** |
| **Task Automation** | Makefile / Shell | Python recipes | Batch / UAT | Cargo | Shell | **Justfile (`just`)** |

entries.title: DEPOT_ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
Developed by Martin von Zweigbergk at Google (`jj-vcs/jj`), Jujutsu is a Git-compatible version control system written in Rust:
- **Working Copy as a Commit**: The working directory is always an automatic commit (`@`). No staging index is needed.
- **Anonymous Branching**: Commits exist without named branches; branch pointers ("bookmarks") are updated smoothly.
- **Conflict-Free Operations**: Merge conflicts are first-class commit states that can be committed, pushed, and resolved later without interrupting rebases.
- **Depot Integration**: `depot_tools/jj/scm.py` provides Google's experimental bridge, while `depot` integrates seamlessly with `.jj` repositories.

entries.title: DEPOT_ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
Depot uses `blake3` instead of SHA-1 or SHA-256 for artifact verification:
- Blake3 processes ~15 GB/s with multi-core tree hashing (AVX-512 / AVX2 SIMD), outperforming SHA-256 by 12x.
- Large multi-gigabyte dependencies (Vulkan SDK, CUDA headers, LLVM toolchains) are verified in sub-second times.

---

entries.text:

entries.title: DEPOT_TOOLS_RUST.md
DEPOT_TOOLS_RUST.md
entries.text:
- `eval`: `Exec` / `ParseLocalConfig` / `_gclient_eval` on Ruff's parser: literals, lists,
  tuples, dicts, `Str()`, `Var()`, `+`, `%`, `{var}` expansion with the `_SafeFormatter` rules
  (attribute and item access rejected), duplicate keys and code rejected.
- `condition`: `EvaluateCondition` (recursive string vars, `Str()` literals, cycle detection,
  `and`/`or` evaluating every operand like `any()`/`all()`).
- `deps`: `Parse` (standardized deps, `deps_os` into conditions, `hooks_os`).
- `tree`: `GClient`/`Dependency` semantics: `.gclient` (`target_os[_only]`, `target_cpu`,
  `cache_dir`, `custom_deps`, `custom_vars`, `custom_hooks`), built-in vars, variable precedence
  (DEPS, parents, built-ins, custom_vars), `recursedeps`, `use_relative_paths`, parent conditions
  ANDed into children, CIPD packages (`version_file` too), GCS objects with merged conditions,
  relative URLs, duplicate detection.
- `revinfo [--deps OS] [--filter X] [--ignore-dep-type T] [--output-json F]`.
- `getdep --var V -r path -r path:package`, `setdep --var k=v -r path@rev -r path:pkg@ver`
  (edits one string literal per change, keeps quotes; `AddVar` placement as upstream; gitlinks for
  `git_dependencies = 'SYNC'` updated through gix-index with the tree cache dropped).
- `sync [--apply] [-j N] [--only P] [--with-solutions] [--cipd]`: dry run by default. Plan: clone,
  fetch, checkout, up to date, unpinned, blocked (non-git directory or local changes), CIPD, GCS.
  Executor on gix: new checkouts are `gix init` + `objects/info/alternates` into the git cache
  mirror (`git clone --shared`), missing commits are fetched over HTTPS by id (Gerrit and GitHub
  serve reachable commits), existing checkouts refuse local changes, then the pinned tree is
  checked out and HEAD detached. Nested checkouts run after their parents, in parallel per level.
- `hooks`: every hook with its expanded action, cwd and whether its condition holds.
- `ay fetch <config> [--prop=value] [--apply]`: all 43 `fetch_configs` (including aliases such
  as `android`, `ios`, `webrtc_android`) as data, the `.gclient` text `fetch.py` writes, then a
  two-pass sync (solutions, then their deps).

Test evidence (`cargo test -p depot-gclient`; the upstream comparisons are `--ignored` because
they run depot_tools' bundled Python 3.11):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `revinfo` vs `python gclient.py revinfo` on `third_party/chromium` | byte-identical for the host default and `--deps=all`, `unix,android`, `mac,ios`, `chromeos,fuchsia` (248, 355, 294, 243, 219 lines; SHA-256 `80c7d1e6...` for the default) |
| Speed, `revinfo` on chromium | 0.20 s (debug build) vs 5.9 s upstream |
| `setdep` vs upstream on a copy of chromium's DEPS | byte-identical for a git dep, a CIPD package, an existing var and a new var. Upstream crashes (`KeyError (3102, 75)`) when a new `--var` and `-r` are combined in one call; ours does not |
| `fetch_configs/*.py fetch` JSON vs ours | identical for all 43 configs, with no props, `--target_os=android,ios` and `--internal=True` |
| Real sync, scratch root with chromium pins | `ced`, `cld_3`, `colorama` from the cache in 0.28 s; `safeint` (not cached) fetched over HTTPS by id in 2.6 s; `git fsck` clean, `git status` empty, HEAD at the pin |
| Real sync in `third_party/chromium` | `src/third_party/snappy/src` and `src/third_party/openh264rs/src` moved to their new pins; `git status` empty and HEAD at the pin |
| Bug found and fixed on that run | gix 0.61 `overwrite_existing` does not truncate files, so shrunk files kept their old tail (21 files in openh264rs). The executor now deletes changed files first; regression test `sync::tests::checkout_replaces_existing_tree` |
| gix 0.61 loose refs and detached HEAD lack the trailing LF | normalized after each write (`git fsck` `refMissingNewline` warnings gone) |

entries.title: DEPOT_TOOLS_RUST.md
entries.text:
Finds the spec like upstream (explicit `--vpy-spec`, the script's PEP 723 block, else the nearest
`vpython.toml`), then runs `uv run --no-project --python <requires-python> --with-requirements
<spec>.uv.lock python ...`. Locks that pin `+chromium.N` wheels (Chromium's own builds, served only
by its wheel index) go to upstream `vpython3` unless `--index-url` / `$AY_VPY_INDEX_URL` names that
index. Real run: `build/mcp_servers/vpython.toml` resolved and imported `mcp` on Python 3.11.18
(23 packages); the root `//vpython.toml` (11 `+chromium` pins) is routed upstream.

repository root, `PATH`, then `C:\depot_tools` (the hard-coded duplicate `C:\src` path is gone),
runs wrappers by full path and sets `DEPOT_TOOLS_UPDATE=0`. `build_tools::use_siso` reproduces
autoninja's choice (`args.gn`, `.sisoenv` plus `.gn` / `gclient_args.gni` / `.siso_deps`, unless

entries.title: DEPOT_TOOLS_RUST.md
entries.text:
[EpicGames/lore](https://github.com/EpicGames/lore) (MIT, `aphrody-dev/lore`, `third_party/lore`) is a centralized, content-addressed VCS for code plus large binaries. Its client and server stay a separate tool; depot_tools takes its storage model, not its protocol, so Git and gclient stay the wire formats.

| Lore idea | Lore source | Here |
|---|---|---|
| FastCDC v2020 fragments, 32/64/256 KiB, normalization 1 | `lore-storage/src/chunker.rs`, `lore-base/src/types` | `crates/depot-cas`, same parameters, test asserts whole-buffer boundaries |
| blake3 fragment ids, immutable store, zstd level 6 | `lore-storage/src/{hash,compress,immutable_store}.rs` | `fragments/<2>/<64 hex>` zstd frames, atomic rename, never rewritten |
| Sparse, on-demand hydration | `lore-fuse`, `lore-revision` | GCS objects and CIPD instances hydrate from the store by sha256 with no network; next: `ay up` archives |
| Dedup across versions | fragment store | sysroot and clang pins share fragments between rolls and between checkouts |

Measured on `third_party/chromium` (Windows, debug `ay`): clang (53 MB) and the Rust toolchain (428 MB) downloaded and extracted in 3 m 33 s; removing `llvm-build/Release+Asserts` and syncing again hydrates it from the store in 17 s with no network. `_content_names` is byte-identical to Python `json.dumps(tarfile.getnames())` for both, so upstream `gclient sync` sees the objects as current. Store: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\depot_tools\cas`, override with `DEPOT_CAS`.

entries.title: DEPOT_TOOLS_RUST.md
entries.text:
Inventory of every git call in our own code (Rust `Command::new("git")`, TypeScript
`Bun.spawn`/`execSync`, just, PowerShell; the Go code in `infra/` never calls git). Coverage is
for gix 0.61 (workspace), gix 0.90 (gitoxide main) and jj 0.46.

| Subcommand | Our call sites | gix 0.61 | gix 0.90 | jj 0.46 | `ay` today |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rev-parse HEAD` / `<ref>` / `--abbrev-ref HEAD` / `--short=N` | 15 (worktree.rs, fork.rs, xtask, forge, vcs-meta-plugin) | yes | yes | `jj log -T` | `ay git rev-parse` on gix; `ForkManager`, `WorktreeManager::add` use gix |
| `branch --show-current` | 2 (xtask, vcs-meta-plugin) | yes | yes | n/a (no current branch) | `ay git branch --show-current` on gix |
| `remote -v` / `get-url` | 5 (fork.rs, xtask, pillars.ts, triforge.ts) | yes | yes | `jj git remote list` | `ay git remote [-v] / get-url` on gix; `ForkManager` uses gix |
| `remote add` / `set-url` / `config <k> <v>` / `--unset-all` | 9 (fork.rs, triforge.ts, git_slim.rs) | config write via `gix-config` file API | same | `jj git remote add/set-url` | still git |
| `config --get` | 2 | yes | yes | `jj config get` | `ay git config --get` on gix |
| `rev-list --left-right --count A...B` | 1 (fork.rs) | yes (rev walk) | yes | revsets | `ay git rev-list` on gix; `ForkManager` uses gix |
| `log -n`, `--pretty` | 5 | yes | yes | `jj log` | `ay git log [-n N] [rev]` on gix (short id + subject only) |
| `status --porcelain` | 3 | index-worktree only | full | `jj status` | `ay git status --porcelain` on gix (tracked changes; no untracked, no index-vs-HEAD) |
| `worktree list` | 1 (worktree.rs) | yes | yes | `jj workspace list` | `ay git worktree list` on gix |
| `worktree add` / `remove` / `prune` | 4 | no | no | `jj workspace add/forget` | still git |
| `fetch` (https) | 4 | yes | yes | `jj git fetch` | `ay gclient sync` fetches on gix; fork sync still git |
| `clone` full | in `ay gclient sync` / `ay fetch` | yes | yes | `jj git clone` | gix |
| `clone --filter=blob:none` / `tree:0`, `--sparse`, `sparse-checkout set` | 6 (git_slim.rs, install.ps1, depot-orgs.ts, sync-ecosystem-submodules.ts) | no partial clone | no partial clone | no | still git |
| `checkout <rev>` (detached) | gclient sync | yes (index from tree + worktree-state) | yes | `jj new <rev>` | gix |
| `checkout -- <file>` | 2 (bun-parity) | yes (blob write) | yes | `jj restore` | still git |
| `update-index --cacheinfo 160000,...` | 1 (sync-ecosystem-submodules.ts) | yes (gix-index) | yes | no | `ay gclient setdep` gitlinks on gix |
| `merge --ff-only` | 1 (fork.rs) | ref update + checkout | yes | `jj rebase`/`jj new` | still git |
| `merge` (true merge) | 1 | no | tree merge yes | yes | still git |
| `rebase` | 1 | no | no | `jj rebase` | still git; jj is the path |
| `push` (incl. multi-forge) | 1 (triforge.ts) | no | no | `jj git push` | still git; jj is the path |
| `submodule update --remote --merge` | 1 (sentinel) | read only | read only | no | still git |
| `diff`, `show --stat -p` | 6 | tree diff, no unified text | unified diff yes | `jj diff --git` | still git |
| `apply` | 2 | no | no | no | still git |
| `add .gitmodules` | 1 | index write (low level) | yes | `jj` auto-tracks | still git |
| `reflog expire`, `prune`, `commit-graph write`, `multi-pack-index write`, `scalar register` | 5 (git_slim.rs, vcs.ts) | no | no | `jj util gc` | still git |
| `show-ref --verify` | 1 | yes | yes | `jj bookmark list` | still git |

Other Git for Windows runtime dependencies: `ssh`/`scp` in `infra/internal/providers/vps.go`
(`ay ssh` on russh replaces them, `crates/remote`), `scalar.exe` (`git_slim.rs`), credential
helpers (`git-credential-luci`, gcloud helper in `triforge.ts`; plan: keyring-backed storage),
cargo's `net.git-fetch-with-cli = true` in `install.ps1`/`install.sh` (cargo can use its built-in
gitoxide/libgit2 fetch instead), and bash for `install.sh`/`deploy.sh` (their pwsh twins exist).
gix's own transports still spawn `ssh` for `ssh://` URLs and `git-upload-pack`

entries.title: ECOSYSTEM_CHOICES.md
entries.text:
- Microsoft Pragmatic Rust Guidelines ([all.txt](https://microsoft.github.io/rust-guidelines/agents/all.txt)):
  - `M-APP-ERROR`: applications use one app error type (`anyhow`). Libraries keep canonical error structs
    (`thiserror`).
  - `M-MIMALLOC-APPS`: applications set mimalloc as the global allocator.
  - `M-CARGO-WORKSPACE`: shared dependencies go in `[workspace.dependencies]` with `default-features = false`.
  - `M-OOBE`: a crate builds with only cargo and rustc. This favours `ring` and pure-Rust codecs over cmake or
    nasm C builds.
  - `M-STATIC-VERIFICATION`: clippy, cargo-audit, cargo-hack, udeps and miri run as gates.
- Chromium (`third_party/chromium/src/third_party/rust/README-importing-new-crates.md`, local mirror):
  - Every crates.io import goes through `gnrt` and is vendored.
  - A shipping crate that contains `unsafe` needs a security review against the rule of 2; crates that fail it
    are confined to the `sandbox` group. We apply the same idea: prefer crates with `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`
    or small audited `unsafe`, and run `cargo deny` / `cargo audit` (both installed in `~/.cargo/bin`).
- Linux kernel Rust ([docs.kernel.org/rust](https://docs.kernel.org/rust/index.html)) does not pull from
  crates.io and builds against pinned in-tree crates. The lesson here is to pin and vendor, not which crates to
  pick.
- [blessed.rs](https://blessed.rs/crates) recommendations:
  - HTTP and async: `reqwest` / `ureq`, `axum` ("recommend for most new projects"), `tokio`.
  - Crypto and TLS: `rustls`.
  - CLI: `clap`, with `bpaf` and `lexopt` as alternatives.
  - Terminal: `ratatui` plus `crossterm`, `indicatif`.
  - Errors: `anyhow` / `thiserror`.
  - Other: `jiff` for time, `tracing` for logging, `directories` / `etcetera` for platform directories.
- Awesome lists checked:
  - [awesome-rust](https://github.com/rust-unofficial/awesome-rust) lists russh, boringtun, rustic, bollard,
    hickory, smithay, ratatui, bottom, keyring, sysinfo, youki, brush, nushell and rclone.
  - [awesome-sysadmin](https://github.com/awesome-foss/awesome-sysadmin) lists restic, rclone and coolify.
  - [awesome-selfhosted](https://github.com/awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted) lists infisical and vector.
  - [awesome-wayland](https://github.com/natpen/awesome-wayland) lists smithay.
  - [awesome-tuis](https://github.com/rothgar/awesome-tuis) lists ratatui and bottom.
  - Also checked: [awesome-cli-apps](https://github.com/agarrharr/awesome-cli-apps),
    [awesome-wasm](https://github.com/mbasso/awesome-wasm) and
    [awesome-bun](https://github.com/apvarun/awesome-bun).
- Repo constraints:
  - Bun built-ins come before npm on the web side (`CLAUDE.md`).
  - The Go deploy engine (`infra/go.mod`) has zero dependencies and calls provider REST APIs directly.
  - `crates/remote` already chose `ring` over `aws-lc-rs` so it needs no cmake or nasm on Windows or musl.
  - Windows links use `rust-lld` and sccache is disabled for incremental builds
    ([`BUILD_SPEED.md`](./BUILD_SPEED.md)).

entries.title: ECOSYSTEM_CHOICES.md
entries.text:
1. Upgrade `ureq` 2.12 to 3.5.1 in `[workspace.dependencies]`. It is used by `crates/up` and others and is
   the network base for every provider verb. Keep the ring-backed `rustls`; add `platform-verifier`.
2. Ship `ay` through **dist** 0.34.0, with self-update via **axoupdater** 0.10.3 (`ay self update`). This gives
   msvc, musl and macOS archives, installers and receipts.
3. Store secrets with **keyring-core** 1.0.1 and the native store crates (`ay secret get/set`). Use **age**
   0.12.1 for files and headless hosts; use sops for anything committed.
4. Build `ay remote exec` fanout on the existing **russh** 0.65.1 and **russh-sftp** 3.0.1: a JoinSet with a
   concurrency cap, `indicatif` 0.18.6 `MultiProgress`, plus `russh-config` and `pageant` for `~/.ssh/config`
   and the Windows agent.
5. Install and run services with **service-manager** 0.11.0, **windows-service** 0.8.1 and **sd-notify** 0.5.0
   (`ay service install/start/status` on Windows, systemd and launchd).
6. Add **object_store** 0.14.2 (R2, S3, GCS) for artifacts and `ay up` mirrors, and keep **rclone** as the
   external sync CLI.
7. Embed **ubi** 0.13.0 in `ay up` for GitHub-release binaries, instead of hand-rolled asset matching.
   `src.lock.json` stays the truth.
8. Supervise child processes with **process-wrap** 10.0.1 (whole-tree kill via Job Objects / process groups)
   for `ay deploy`, `ay test` and `ay wl` children.
9. Load config with **config** 0.15.27 (`ay.toml` plus `AY_` environment overrides) and write with
   **toml_edit** 0.25.
10. Back up with **rustic_core** 0.13.0 (`ay backup`), restic-compatible.
11. Schedule with **croner** 4.0.3 plus tokio (`ay cron`); use apalis only if durable queues appear.
12. Export telemetry with **opentelemetry-otlp** 0.33.1 and **tracing-opentelemetry** 0.34.0 behind a
    feature flag; run Vector on hosts.
13. Set **mimalloc** 0.1.52 as the global allocator of the `ay` binary (`M-MIMALLOC-APPS`).
14. Use **bollard** 0.21.1 for `ay deploy` local image builds and inspection; use oci-client 0.18.0 for
    registry pushes without a daemon.
15. Use **hickory-resolver** 0.26.3 for `ay net dns` diagnostics (DoH, DNSSEC, record types beyond A/AAAA).

entries.title: ENGINE-DECISION.md
entries.text:
**Couches (de bas en haut)**
1. **`aphrody-v8`** : fork `aphrody-labs/rusty_v8`.
   - Son sous-module `v8/` pointe sur `v8_revision` du DEPS de `C:\src`. `build/`, `buildtools/` et `third_party/*` sont alignés sur `v8/DEPS` à cette révision.
   - Build avec `V8_FROM_SOURCE=1`, et `GN`, `NINJA` pris dans `C:\src\third_party\depot_tools`. Le clang est celui de Chromium (`CLANG_BASE_PATH` = `third_party/llvm-build`), `SCCACHE` vient de `src.lock.json`.
   - Un `.lib` statique est produit et mis en cache par hash de révision via `RUSTY_V8_ARCHIVE`.
2. **`aphrody-core`** : fork `aphrody-labs/deno`, extrait de `libs/core` (+ `serde_v8`, `ops` macro).
   - Il porte l'event loop, les ops `#[op2(fast)]`, les modules ESM et le snapshot.
   - Reste ouvert : soit réduire `deno_core` au nécessaire, soit écrire notre propre couche mince. Il faut décider sur mesure (taille, nombre d'ops).
3. **`aphrody-io`** : tokio (IOCP / io_uring), hyper et rustls.
   - Les buffers sont des `bytes::Bytes` exposés en `ArrayBuffer` via `v8::ArrayBuffer::new_backing_store_from_bytes` (deleter Rust), donc zero-copy.
4. **APIs** :
   - `aphrody-web` : fetch, Streams, URL, Encoding, WebCrypto via aws-lc-rs ou ring, structuredClone.
   - `aphrody-workers` : modèle isolate par requête, `compatibility_date` et flags, KV/DO/Cache/R2 en local, `nodejs_compat`.
   - `aphrody-node` : polyfills repris de Deno `ext/node`, sous MIT.
5. **Outils** :
   - `aphrody-bundler` : oxc, rolldown, lightningcss et le port Tailwind v4.
   - `aphrody-vercel` : Build Output API v3 (`.vercel/output`, functions edge/node, prerender, ISR).
   - `aphrody-next` : RSC et Flight, middleware edge.
   - `aphrody-pm`, `aphrody-test`.
6. **`lore*`** : inchangé.
7. **`aphrody-render`** (feature `render`, désactivée par défaut) : blitz-dom/html/paint, stylo non modifié et `vello_cpu`, sans wgpu ni winit côté serveur. Les pins sont réalignés sur un fork commun.
8. **`crates/conformance`** :
   - test262 via `v8/tools/run-tests.py` sur notre V8 ;
   - WPT runtime (`fetch/`, `streams/`, `url/`, `encoding/`, `WebCryptoAPI/`) contre `aphrody` ;
   - WPT layout de `render` comparé à l'oracle Chromium 160 en CDP ;
   - tests workerd et `bun/test/js/workerd` (HTMLRewriter seulement, couverture limitée).

**Crates**
- Gardées : `cli`, `conformance`, `lore*`.
- Retirées du chemin par défaut : blitz, stylo, vello, wgpu, winit (passent sous `render`). Plus aucun pin `v8 =152.2.0` venant de crates.io.
- Ajoutées : `aphrody-v8`, `aphrody-core`, `aphrody-io`, `aphrody-web`, `aphrody-workers`, `aphrody-node`, `aphrody-bundler`, `aphrody-vercel`, `aphrody-next`, `aphrody-pm`, `aphrody-test`, `aphrody-render`.

**Politique de révision V8**
- La seule source de vérité est `C:\src\DEPS` `v8_revision`, qui suit le pin Chromium dans `src.lock.json`.
- Une recette `just v8-roll` :
  1. lit la révision ;
  2. met à jour le sous-module du fork ;
  3. synchronise les deps V8 ;
  4. build ;
  5. lance `cargo test -p aphrody-v8` ;
  6. lance test262.
- On roll quand Chromium bouge, au rythme des branches et non de HEAD brut.
- Un tag `aphrody-v8-<v8ver>` (aujourd'hui 16.0.25) est créé à chaque roll.
- Sémantique Workers : un écart de version avec workerd (15.8.62.5) est acceptable, car les flags de compat sont gérés par nous et non par V8.

**Build**
- Cargo est maître. GN et ninja ne servent qu'à l'intérieur du `build.rs` de `aphrody-v8`, avec depot_tools réutilisé tel quel. Aucun gclient ne touche labs.
- Release :
  - `lto="fat"`, `codegen-units=1`, `panic="abort"`, PGO (`cargo pgo` sur des workloads Next et Workers) ;
  - un LTO croisé optionnel : V8 compilé `-flto=thin` + `-Clinker-plugin-lto` avec le même LLVM que le rustc nightly. Le gain est à mesurer avant de l'adopter.
- AOT et démarrage :
  - startup snapshot contenant web, workers et node pré-initialisés (`JsRuntimeForSnapshot` dans `build.rs`) ;
  - code cache V8 par module bundle ;
  - pool d'isolates pré-chauffés.
- Zero-copy : fast API calls, `String::new_ext

entries.title: ENGINE-DECISION.md
entries.text:
1. Corriger les docs : V8 local = 16.0.25 (`v8-version.h`), `deno_core` archivé mais publié depuis `deno/libs/core`. Fichiers : `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` et `docs/ROADMAP.md`. Vérification : grep « 15.9 » renvoie 0 résultat.
2. Mesurer la base : `cargo build --release` avec le prébuilt `v8 152.2.0`, `hyperfine 'aphrody -e ""'`, taille du binaire. Résultats consignés dans `docs/CONFORMANCE.md`.
3. Forker `denoland/rusty_v8` en `aphrody-labs/rusty_v8`, avec une branche `v8-16.0.25` dont le sous-module est `e4e354fb…`. Synchroniser les deps V8 (`gclient` avec le `.gclient` de V8, ou un script `tools/update_deps` du fork).
4. Build de `V8_FROM_SOURCE=1` avec `GN`, `NINJA` et `CLANG_BASE_PATH` pris dans `C:\src\third_party`, et `SCCACHE=sccache`. Corriger `src/binding.cc` jusqu'au vert. Critère : `cargo test` passe sur le fork, et la durée du build à froid comme celle de l'incrémental sont notées.
5. Patcher le workspace : `v8 = { git = "aphrody-labs/rusty_v8", rev = … }`, `deno_core` aligné. Vérifier `cargo tree -i v8` (une seule version) et `cargo deny check`.
6. Passer blitz, stylo, vello et wgpu sous la feature `render`. Vérifier que `cargo tree -e normal` sans features ne contient plus `stylo` et que deny reste vert.
7. Ajouter la recette `just v8-roll` : elle lit `C:\src\DEPS`, met à jour le sous-module, build, puis lance test262. Pour vérifier, la lancer deux fois de suite : la seconde ne fait rien, la révision étant déjà à jour.
8. Créer le snapshot et `aphrody-web` minimal (fetch, Streams, URL, Encoding). Faire tourner WPT runtime en CI et publier le score.
9. Écrire `aphrody-workers` (isolate par requête, compat_date), puis porter les tests workerd fetch et streams.
10. Écrire `aphrody-vercel` : Build Output v3 sur un exemple `vercel/examples`, puis un deploy de test.
11. Next.js App Router : `next start` sous `aphrody`, avec le diff visuel de l'oracle `headless_shell` en CDP.
12. Puis PGO, et le test du LTO croisé (`-Clinker-plugin-lto`) : on ne le garde que si le gain est d'au moins 5 % sur les benchs de l'étape 2.

entries.title: ENGINE-DECISION.md
entries.text:
**Chromium : rôles séparés**
- Le checkout `C:\src\third_party\chromium\src` (Chromium 160.0.8158.0, V8 16.0.25) sert uniquement de source à extraire : `third_party/*`, LLVM/clang, documentation, ressources UI. Il n'est ni embarqué ni ciblé, car 160 est incompatible avec les embeddings ci-dessous.
- Cibles d'embedding (VPS et desktop), toujours sur la dernière version publiée :
  - CEF via `tauri-apps/cef-rs` 156.4.0+156.0.26 (Chromium 156) ;
  - Tauri v3 (`tauri-v3.0.0-alpha.6`) ;
  - Electron 43.8.9 (Chromium 150.0.7871.250).
- La politique de révision V8 change : `aphrody-v8` suit le V8 du Chromium de cef-rs (la cible d'embedding la plus récente), et non la HEAD du checkout. Le JS côté serveur garde ainsi la même sémantique que le navigateur livré. `just v8-roll` lit la version Chromium dans `cef-rs`.

**Priorités produit dès la création**
- WebAssembly et WebGPU sont des cibles de premier rang : le runtime expose WASM (SIMD, threads, GC, exceptions, memory64, JSPI) et WebGPU via `wgpu` (et Dawn comme référence). Le pipeline build produit du WASM optimisé (`wasm-opt`/binaryen, `wasm-bindgen`).
- Front supporté de bout en bout : TypeScript (tsc et `typescript-go`), Tailwind v4, shadcn, Base UI, React, Svelte, Solid, Vue, vanilla JS, Electron, Microsoft Fluent UI/FAST, et les APIs Bun (HTML/CSS bundler, React).
- Équivalents Rust suivis et forkés : GPUI (Zed), gpui-component, Tauri v3, Taffy, Leptos, Axum, Blitz, wasmtime.

entries.title: EPIC_GAMES_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
Unreal Engine `.pak` files store their primary directory index metadata at the **end of the file** within a standardized footer structure:

```text
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| File Payload 0 | File Payload 1 | ... | Primary Directory Index Table |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                        ^                               ^
                                        | Index Offset                  | Footer (FPakInfo)
```

#### The `FPakInfo` Footer Layout (Magic: `0x5A6F12E1` / `1517228769` Little-Endian)
The footer is read backwards from the end of the file (varying from 44 to 228 bytes depending on PAK version):

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `EncryptionKeyGuid` | `[u8; 16]` | GUID identifying the AES-256 decryption key for encrypted archives |
| `EncryptedIndex` | `u8` | `1` if the primary index is AES-256 encrypted, `0` if plaintext |
| `Magic` | `u32` | `0x5A6F12E1` (`PAK_FILE_MAGIC`) validating archive integrity |
| `Version` | `u32` | PAK format version (1 to 11; UE 4.0..4.27 uses v7..v8, UE 5.0+ uses v11) |
| `IndexOffset` | `u64` | Byte offset from the start of the file where the index table begins |
| `IndexSize` | `u64` | Byte length of the serialized index table |
| `IndexHash` | `[u8; 20]` | SHA-1 hash of the index table |
| `CompressionMethods` | `[u8; 128]` | Array of 4-byte ANSI compression method names (`Oodle`, `Zlib`, `Gzip`, `LZ4`, `Zstd`) |

---

entries.title: EPIC_GAMES_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
Unreal Engine serialized packages are split into:
1. `.uasset`: Package header, name map, import table, and export table metadata.
2. `.uexp`: Package binary export data (bytecode, textures, mesh vertices).
3. `.ubulk`: Optional uncompressed streaming data (mipmaps, audio streams).

#### Package File Summary Header (Magic: `0x9E2A83C1` / `-1641380927`)
| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Tag` | `i32` | `0x9E2A83C1` (`PACKAGE_FILE_TAG`) |
| `LegacyFileVersion` | `i32` | Negative integer representing engine version (e.g. `-7` for UE4/UE5) |
| `LegacyUE3Version` | `i32` | Legacy UE3 version flag (typically `0` or `864`) |
| `FileVersionUE4` | `i32` | File version enum (e.g. `522` for UE 4.27, `524` for UE 5.3) |
| `FileVersionUE5` | `i32` | File version enum for UE5 features |
| `FileVersionLicensee` | `i32` | Custom licensee file version |
| `CustomVersions` | `Array` | List of GUID + Version pairs tracking engine feature flags |
| `TotalHeaderSize` | `i32` | Total byte size of `.uasset` header before `.uexp` export payload |
| `FolderName` | `String` | Package mount path (e.g. `/Game/Characters/Hero`) |
| `PackageFlags` | `u32` | Bitmask (`PKG_FilterEditorOnly`, `PKG_CompiledIn`, etc.) |
| `NameCount` / `NameOffset` | `i32, i32` | Count and byte offset to the Name Map table |
| `ImportCount` / `ImportOffset` | `i32, i32` | Count and byte offset to the Import Table |
| `ExportCount` / `ExportOffset` | `i32, i32` | Count and byte offset to the Export Table |

---

   POST https://account-public-service-prod03.ol.epicgames.com/account/api/oauth/token
   Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
   Authorization: Basic <base64(client_id:client_secret)>

2. **Entitlements & Asset Discovery**:

entries.title: EPIC_GAMES_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
EGS games are distributed as content-addressed chunk streams governed by a binary manifest:
- **Magic Signature**: `0x0b83c027` (JSON-header binary format) or `0x0b83c026`.
- **Chunk Catalog**: Contains a list of all content chunks identified by a 64-bit chunk GUID and a 32-bit CRC or SHA-1 hash.
- **File Manifest**: Maps logical game file paths (e.g. `Engine/Binaries/Win64/UnrealEditor.exe`) to an ordered list of chunks with byte offsets and sizes.
- **CDN Base URL**: Chunks are fetched via HTTPS from Akamai, Fastly, or Cloudflare CDNs:
  ```text
  https://content-cache.epicgames.com/Builds/{namespace}/{appName}/CloudDir/ChunksV4/{hash_prefix}/{chunk_guid}.chunk
  ```

---

entries.title: EPIC_GAMES_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
- **Platform Interface**: Manages thread loop (`EOS_Platform_Tick`), memory allocations, and network logging.
- **Auth Interface**: Supports account link, persistent login, and OpenID Connect tokens.
- **P2P Interface**: Encrypted, NAT-punched peer-to-peer data transport over WebRTC / DTLS.
- **Lobby & Matchmaking**: Cloud-coordinated session discovery and search filters.

entries.title: EPIC_GAMES_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
EAC client modules are distributed from the official Epic Games EAC CDN:
```text
https://modules-cdn.eac-prod.on.epicgames.com/modules/{game_guid}/{platform}/eac_module.bin
```
The payload is encrypted with an 8-byte rolling chain-cipher inspected via `crates/shenron-re/src/fs/eac.rs` and `crates/corelib::re`.

2. **`crates/depot`**:

entries.title: EPIC_GAMES_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
Unreal Engine models world space in centimeters using a Left-Handed, Z-Up basis:
- UE $X$ is Forward
- UE $Y$ is Right
- UE $Z$ is Up

Bevy ECS models world space in meters using a Right-Handed, Y-Up basis:
- Bevy $X = \text{UE } Y \times 0.01$ (Right)
- Bevy $Y = \text{UE } Z \times 0.01$ (Up)
- Bevy $Z = -\text{UE } X \times 0.01$ (Backwards)

This transformation is implemented with zero-copy vector arithmetic in `crates/corelib::epic::BevyTransform::from_unreal_coords`.

entries.title: EPIC_GAMES_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
Unreal Engine fighting games (e.g. Dragon Ball FighterZ, Guilty Gear Strive) use the Arc System Works cel-shading technique backed by ILM (Intermediate Light Map) textures:
- **Red Channel**: Specular highlight / metallic mask.
- **Green Channel**: Ambient occlusion / shadow ramp bias threshold.
- **Blue Channel**: Line art mask / crease multiplier.
- **Alpha Channel**: Surface glossiness / outline thickness weight.
- **Normal Steering**: Inverted hull vertex normals are steered using vertex color RGB offsets to prevent geometry breaks on faceted edges.

The WGSL cel-shading pipeline is verified in `apps/shenron/packages/engine/src/shaders/arcsys-cel.wgsl.ts` and encapsulated in `corelib::epic::ArcSysCelMaterial`.

entries.title: EPIC_GAMES_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
The backend provides deterministic simulation and asset distribution:
- `GET /api/game/bevy/health`: Engine metadata, 60 FPS deterministic tick rate, and coordinate convention.
- `GET /api/game/bevy/scene?character=...`: Returns serialized `BevySceneBundle` converted from `.uasset`.
- `POST /api/game/bevy/tick`: Deterministic 60 Hz frame step advancing `SimulationClock` with clamped delta accumulator and bitmask input validation.
