entries.title: INSTALL_UPDATE.md
entries.text:
`ay` is the package `aphrody` (crates/ay). It is the only workspace member dist builds:
`dist-workspace.toml` sets `dist = false` for everyone and `crates/ay/Cargo.toml` opts back in with
`[package.metadata.dist] dist = true`. Targets: `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`,
`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`,
`aarch64-apple-darwin`. Installers: shell and PowerShell, both installing into `~/.local/bin`
(`install-path`), the same directory `ay up` manages. Builds use `[profile.dist]` in the root
`Cargo.toml`, which inherits `release` (fat LTO, one codegen unit, abort, stripped).

Release steps:

1. Bump `[workspace.package] version` in the root `Cargo.toml` and the `ay` pin in `tools.toml`.
2. `dist plan` must list `aphrody-<target>.{zip,tar.xz}` with `.sha256` files and both installers.
3. Push the tag `v<version>`. `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds every target, uploads the
   archives, `sha256.sum`, `source.tar.gz` and `aphrody-installer.{sh,ps1}` to a GitHub Release on
   `aphrody-dev/src`.

The workflow is generated by `dist generate` with one manual patch: every `actions/checkout` step
gets `token: ${{ secrets.SUBMODULES_TOKEN || github.token }}`, because `crates/bench`,
`crates/ring3-agent`, `crates/rust-stack` and some `apps/*` are private submodules that the
default `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot read (and the workspace glob `crates/*` needs them). Create the
secret once with a read-only token for `aphrody-dev` and `aphrody-labs`
(`gh secret set SUBMODULES_TOKEN -R aphrody-dev/src`). `allow-dirty = ["ci"]` keeps `dist plan`
from rejecting the patch; re-apply it after any `dist generate`.

First install on a fresh machine (public release assets):

```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/aphrody-dev/src/releases/latest/download/aphrody-installer.sh | sh
```

```powershell
irm https://github.com/aphrody-dev/src/releases/latest/download/aphrody-installer.ps1 | iex
```

While `aphrody-dev/src` is private, release assets need a token: either copy a `ay` built with
`ay build --target linux-musl --release`, or download with `gh release download v<version> -R aphrody-dev/src`.

entries.title: INSTALL_UPDATE.md
entries.text:
`ay self-update` embeds axoupdater (blocking API). With a dist install receipt it reuses the
receipt's source and install prefix; without one (a binary built from source or placed by `ay up`)
it targets GitHub Releases of `aphrody-dev/src`, app `aphrody`, the current version from the
binary, and the directory of the running executable. It downloads the release's
`aphrody-installer.{sh,ps1}` and runs it with the install directory forced, so the result is the
same as a fresh install. `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` are passed to the release lookup.

- `ay self-update --check`: exit 0 when current, 1 when a newer release exists.
- `ay self-update --version 0.3.0`: install that version (also downgrades).

Limitation: the dist installer script downloads its archive anonymously, so on a private repo the
lookup succeeds and the install fails. `ay up ay` covers that case: it downloads the pinned
release through the GitHub API with the token.

entries.title: INSTALL_UPDATE.md
entries.text:
`tools.toml` lists every tool with a pinned version, the executables it provides, a version probe
and one source:

| Source | Used for | Install |
|---|---|---|
| `github` | ay, bun, gh, ovhcloud, coreutils, ripgrep, just, cargo-zigbuild, dist | release asset per platform, executables copied into `bin_dir` |
| `url` | gcloud, zig | direct archive; `layout = "tree"` unpacks under `tools_dir/<name>/<version>` and links `bin` entries into `bin_dir` |
| `bun` | wrangler, hostinger-api-mcp | `bun add --global <package>@<version>` (Bun's own `~/.bun`) |
| `installer` | rustup | `rustup-init -y --no-modify-path --default-toolchain none`; an existing rustup runs `rustup self update` |
| `ubi` | fd, dust, bat, delta, sd, hyperfine, tokei, watchexec, zoxide, eza, xh, yq, jj, sccache, uv, caddy, cloudflared, rclone, cargo-binstall, cargo-nextest, gitoxide | the `ubi` crate picks the asset for the OS/arch at the pinned tag and installs the executable into `bin_dir`; `matching.<os>` breaks ties (`msvc`, `max-pure`) |

Two installers coexist on purpose. `github` / `url` entries name the exact asset per platform and
verify sha256; they cover the tools that matter for builds, deploys and the hosts. `ubi` entries
need only `repo` and a tag, which keeps 21 general CLI tools to a few lines each, but ubi 0.13
verifies no checksum (the install line says so). Move a tool from `ubi` to `github` when its
integrity matters. The ubi pins match what the workstation already has, so `ay up` adds no second
copy next to the winget or cargo one.

Versions with `lock = "<key>"` (bun, just, zig) come from `src.lock.json` `toolchains.<key>` when
the repository is present. Manifest lookup order: `--manifest`, `$AY_TOOLS_MANIFEST`,
`<repo>/tools.toml` (repo found through `$SRC_ROOT` or the nearest `src.lock.json`), then the copy
embedded in the binary at build time, which is what hosts without a checkout use.

States: `ok`, `ahead` (newer than the pin, left alone), `outdated`, `missing`, `unknown` (version
unreadable), `n/a` (no asset for this platform). `ay up --check` prints the table and exits 1 when
any tool is `missing` or `outdated`. `ay up` acts on exactly those, then probes again;
`--dry-run` prints the download URLs instead.

Rules the installer enforces:

- Writes only under the user's home: `bin_dir` (default `~/.local/bin`, `AY_BIN_DIR` overrides),
  `tools_dir` (`~/.local/share/ay/tools`), Bun's global directory, rustup's `~/.cargo`.
  Destinations under `%WINDIR%` (including `C:\Windows\System32`), `Program Files`, `/usr`, `/bin`,
  `/sbin`, `/lib`, `/etc` and `/opt` are refused.
- A tool found outside `bin_dir` at the right version is left where it is (winget, Program Files,
  `~/.cargo/bin`). An outdated one gets a fresh copy in `bin_dir`, which must come first on `PATH`.
- Binary tools are probed as real executables (`rg.exe`, never an unrelated `rg.cmd` shim).
- sha256 is verified whenever upstream publishes it: release checksum files (`SHA256SUMS`,
  `SHASUMS256.txt`, `gh_<v>_checksums.txt`), per-asset `.sha256`, `{url}.sha256` (rustup), or
  hashes pinned in `tools.toml` (zig, from `ziglang.org/download/index.json`). coreutils and
  gcloud publish none; the output says `no checksum published`.
- Running executables are replaced by rename (`.ay-old`), so `ay up` can update `ay.exe` itself.
- `ay up --check` prints `note:` lines for duplicates (the same tool at several PATH entries, e.g.
  bun from winget and `~/.bun/bin`) and shadows (a same-name shim winning for cmd/PowerShell, e.g.
  `~/.local/bin/rg.cmd` in front of ripgrep). Notes never change the exit code.
- HTTP is ureq 3 (rustls on ring; `Authorization` is dropped on redirects); archives are read with
  `zip` 9, `tar` + `flate2`, and `lzma-rust2` (xz), all pure Rust. The `ubi` path brings reqwest
  and tokio (shared with axoupdater) plus ubi's own `xz2` and `zstd` C builds (cc only, no cmake).

Adding a tool: append a `[[tool]]` with assets for the five platform keys
(`windows-x86_64`,

entries.title: INSTALL_UPDATE.md
entries.text:
`install.ps1` and `install.sh` stay the entry points for now and are not removed. Every step they
perform has a declarative equivalent in `tools.toml`, applied by `ay up --bootstrap` (tools first,
then the items below, then `ay doctor`). `ay up --check` lists the items with their state (`ok`,
`differs`, `missing`) without counting them in the exit code.

| install.ps1 / install.sh step | `ay up` equivalent |
|---|---|
| `Ensure-Tool` sccache, just, jj, cargo-binstall, cargo-nextest, gix (winget / cargo binstall) | `[[tool]]` entries (`ubi` or `github`), no compile |
| `~/.local/bin` on the user PATH | the dist installer adds it on first install; `ay up` writes nowhere else |
| write `~/.cargo/config.toml` (sccache wrapper, `ay` alias, target-cpu=native) | `[[file]] cargo-config` per OS, created only when missing |
| write the jj config (`%APPDATA%/jj`, `~/.config/jj`) | `[[file]] jj-config` at `{config}/jj/config.toml` |
| clone missing repositories from `src.lock.json` | built in: missing `repositories` entries with an https/ssh URL are cloned `--depth=1 --filter=blob:none` |
| `cargo install --path crates/ay` | the `ay` tool entry (dist release), then `ay self-update` |
| `go build ./cmd/src-deploy` | `[[step]] src-deploy` (runs when `infra/go.mod` exists and the binary is missing) |
| `bun build --compile packages/ai-triad` | `[[step]] triad` |
| `frg.cmd` / bash `frg` shim | `[[step]] frg`: an AOT `bun build --compile` binary instead of a shim |
| `.claude/skills` junction or symlink | `[[link]] claude-skills` (junction on Windows, symlink elsewhere) |
| `ay doctor` | run at the end of `--bootstrap` |
| `cargo build --release` in `crates/rust-stack` | dropped: it is a root workspace member (`cargo build -p rust-stack`) |

Steps run with `RUSTC_WRAPPER` empty: building through sccache crashes rustc on the workstation
(the same reason `just install-ay` needs `RUSTC_WRAPPER=` today).

Once a public `ay` release exists, both scripts shrink to a bootstrap of about ten lines:

```powershell
# install.ps1 (target)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
irm https://github.com/aphrody-dev/src/releases/latest/download/aphrody-installer.ps1 | iex
$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE/.local/bin;$env:PATH"
$env:SRC_ROOT = $PSScriptRoot
ay up --bootstrap
ay up --setup
```

```sh
# install.sh (target)
set -eu
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/aphrody-dev/src/releases/latest/download/aphrody-installer.sh | sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
SRC_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)" ay up --bootstrap
ay up --setup || true
```

entries.title: INSTALL_UPDATE.md
entries.text:
Non-interactive provider wiring. Credentials are read from the process environment first, then
`<repo>/.env` (dotenvy; the process environment is not modified). Values are never printed: they
reach child processes through their environment or stdin, and every printed line is scrubbed of
credential values.

| Provider | Needs | Check | Wiring |
|---|---|---|---|
| GitHub | `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` | `gh auth status` against stored credentials | if not logged in, `gh auth login --with-token` from stdin |
| Cloudflare | `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` | `wrangler whoami` with both in its environment | env only (wrangler reads them per run) |
| Google Cloud | an active gcloud account | `gcloud config get-value account` | if none and `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` is a file, `gcloud auth activate-service-account` |
| OVHcloud | `~/.ovh.conf` | `ovhcloud account get` | none (created by `ovhcloud login`) |
| Hostinger | `HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN` | `GET https://developers.hostinger.com/api/vps/v1/virtual-machines` returns 200 | none |

The table shows the provider, which credential names were found, `ok`/`FAIL` and a masked detail
(`a***@domain` for accounts). Exit 1 when any provider fails.

entries.title: INSTALL_UPDATE.md
entries.text:
`infra/generated/systemd/ay-up.service` and `ay-up.timer` are **user** units, so nothing runs as
root on fr1/fr2 and `%h` resolves to the deploy user's home. They are not deployed by any tool;
install them by hand on each host:

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user ~/.config/ay
cp ay-up.service ay-up.timer ~/.config/systemd/user/
printf 'GH_TOKEN=...\n' > ~/.config/ay/env && chmod 600 ~/.config/ay/env   # only for private releases
loginctl enable-linger "$USER"
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now ay-up.timer
systemctl --user list-timers ay-up.timer
journalctl --user -u ay-up.service
```

Each run (daily, randomized within an hour, catching up after downtime): `ay self-update` first
(failure ignored), then `ay up`. The order matters: the embedded `tools.toml` travels with the
binary, so a new `ay` release is how new tool pins reach hosts. A host with a checkout can follow
the repository instead by setting `SRC_ROOT=/home/ubuntu/src` in `~/.config/ay/env`.

| Host | User | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `usa` (`ssh prd`) | root | production; `ay up --setup` with `HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN` checks the API |
| `fr1` (`ssh vps`) | ubuntu | builds: rustup, zig, cargo-zigbuild, dist matter most |
| `fr2` (`ssh cdn`) | ubuntu | CDN, cron and sync: wrangler and gcloud matter most |

The aarch64 Linux `cargo-zigbuild` asset is a glibc build; the hosts are x86_64 Ubuntu.

entries.title: INSTALL_UPDATE.md
entries.text:
Published files are content-addressed and never overwritten; one small manifest per release says
which objects are current.

1. Build (for wasm: `ay build -t wasm32 --release`, then `wasm-bindgen` into a `pkg/` directory).
2. `ay up --assets <dir> --release <version-or-commit> > manifest.json` hashes every file and
   prints, per logical path, the immutable key `<stem>.<sha256[0..12]>.<ext>`, the full sha256,
   size and content type (`application/wasm` for `.wasm`). Output is sorted and deterministic.
3. Upload each asset under its key once (keys that exist are skipped, so a release only uploads
   what changed), with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`:
   `wrangler r2 object put <bucket>/<key> --file <dir>/<logical> --content-type <type> --cache-control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"`.
4. Upload `manifest.json` last to `<bucket>/<app>/manifest.json` (short `max-age`, e.g. 60 s) and a
   copy to `<bucket>/<app>/releases/<release>.json` for rollback. Rolling back is re-uploading an
   older `releases/<release>.json` as `manifest.json`.
5. Pages and loaders resolve logical names through the manifest, so a deploy is atomic for clients:
   they see either the old manifest and old objects, or the new manifest and new objects.

Buckets per service are in `deploy.toml` (`r2_bucket`); the CDN origin is `fr2`. Garbage
collection of keys no longer referenced by any `releases/*.json` is a later step and not
implemented. Only step 2 is implemented in `ay` today (`crates/up/src/assets.rs`, tested); upload
stays with `wrangler` until the deploy engine takes it over.

entries.title: LUA52_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
1. **`_ENV` Lexical Scope**:
   In Lua 5.1, global variables resided in an environment table associated with the running function or thread via `setfenv`/`getfenv`. In Lua 5.2, `setfenv` and `getfenv` were eliminated. Instead, every chunk is compiled inside an implicit upvalue named `_ENV`. Any reference to a free variable `name` is compiled as `_ENV.name`.

2. **The `goto` and `::label::` Statement**:
   Enables structured state machines and lexically checked jumps without introducing arbitrary spaghetti transitions. A `goto` cannot jump into the scope of a local variable or into another function.

3. **Built-in `bit32` Library**:
   Official 32-bit bitwise library (`band`, `bor`, `bxor`, `bnot`, `lshift`, `rshift`, `arshift`) ensuring cross-platform bitwise parity without external C modules.

4. **Table & Coroutine Improvements**:
   - `table.pack(...)` stores arguments and provides field `n` holding the total parameter count.
   - `table.unpack(t, i, j)` replaced the global `unpack`.
   - `__pairs` and `__ipairs` metamethods for custom table iteration.
   - Coroutine yield through protected calls (`pcall` and `xpcall` can yield in Lua 5.2).

---

entries.title: LUA52_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
Compiled Lua 5.2 chunks carry the `\x1bLua\x52` header. Instructions are 32 bits wide, encoded in one of four modes:
- `ABC`: `opcode (6 bits) | a (8 bits) | c (9 bits) | b (9 bits)`
- `ABx`: `opcode (6 bits) | a (8 bits) | bx (18 bits unsigned)`
- `AsBx`: `opcode (6 bits) | a (8 bits) | sbx (18 bits signed, bias 131,071)`
- `Ax`: `opcode (6 bits) | ax (26 bits unsigned)`

entries.title: LUA52_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
| Opcode | Name | Mode | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `MOVE` | ABC | `R(A) := R(B)` |
| 1 | `LOADK` | ABx | `R(A) := Kst(Bx)` |
| 2 | `LOADKX` | ABx | `R(A) := Kst(extra arg)` |
| 3 | `LOADBOOL` | ABC | `R(A) := (Bool)B; if (C) pc++` |
| 4 | `LOADNIL` | ABC | `R(A), R(A+1), ..., R(A+B) := nil` |
| 5 | `GETUPVAL` | ABC | `R(A) := UpValue[B]` |
| 6 | `GETTABUP` | ABC | `R(A) := UpValue[B][RK(C)]` (Globals) |
| 7 | `GETTABLE` | ABC | `R(A) := R(B)[RK(C)]` |
| 8 | `SETTABUP` | ABC | `UpValue[A][RK(B)] := RK(C)` (Globals) |
| 9 | `SETUPVAL` | ABC | `UpValue[B] := R(A)` |
| 10 | `SETTABLE` | ABC | `R(A)[RK(B)] := RK(C)` |
| 11 | `NEWTABLE` | ABC | `R(A) := {} (size = B,C)` |
| 12 | `SELF` | ABC | `R(A+1) := R(B); R(A) := R(B)[RK(C)]` |
| 13 | `ADD` | ABC | `R(A) := RK(B) + RK(C)` |
| 14 | `SUB` | ABC | `R(A) := RK(B) - RK(C)` |
| 15 | `MUL` | ABC | `R(A) := RK(B) * RK(C)` |
| 16 | `DIV` | ABC | `R(A) := RK(B) / RK(C)` |
| 17 | `MOD` | ABC | `R(A) := RK(B) % RK(C)` |
| 18 | `POW` | ABC | `R(A) := RK(B) ^ RK(C)` |
| 19 | `UNM` | ABC | `R(A) := -R(B)` |
| 20 | `NOT` | ABC | `R(A) := not R(B)` |
| 21 | `LEN` | ABC | `R(A) := length of R(B)` |
| 22 | `CONCAT` | ABC | `R(A) := R(B).. ... ..R(C)` |
| 23 | `JMP` | AsBx | `pc += sBx; if (A) close_upvalues(A-1)` |
| 24 | `EQ` | ABC | `if ((RK(B) == RK(C)) ~= A) pc++` |
| 25 | `LT` | ABC | `if ((RK(B) <  RK(C)) ~= A) pc++` |
| 26 | `LE` | ABC | `if ((RK(B) <= RK(C)) ~= A) pc++` |
| 27 | `TEST` | ABC | `if not (R(A) <=> C) pc++` |
| 28 | `TESTSET` | ABC | `if (R(B) <=> C) { R(A) := R(B) } else pc++` |
| 29 | `CALL` | ABC | `R(A), ... ,R(A+C-2) := R(A)(R(A+1), ... ,R(A+B-1))` |
| 30 | `TAILCALL` | ABC | `return R(A)(R(A+1), ... ,R(A+B-1))` |
| 31 | `RETURN` | ABC | `return R(A), ... ,R(A+B-2)` |
| 32 | `FORLOOP` | AsBx | `R(A)+=R(A+2); if R(A) <?= R(A+1) { pc+=sBx; R(A+3)=R(A) }` |
| 33 | `FORPREP` | AsBx | `R(A)-=R(A+2); pc+=sBx` |
| 34 | `TFORCALL` | ABC | `R(A+3), ... ,R(A+2+C) := R(A)(R(A+1), R(A+2))` |
| 35 | `TFORLOOP` | AsBx | `if R(A+1) ~= nil { R(A)=R(A+1); pc += sBx }` |
| 36 | `SETLIST` | ABC | `R(A)[(C-1)*FPF+i] := R(A+i), 1 <= i <= B` |
| 37 | `CLOSURE` | ABx | `R(A) := closure(KPROTO[Bx])` |
| 38 | `VARARG` | ABC | `R(A), R(A+1), ..., R(A+B-2) = vararg` |
| 39 | `EXTRAARG` | Ax | `extra (larger) argument for previous opcode` |

---

entries.title: LUA52_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
- **WebGPU on Discrete GPU**: `config.front_end = "WebGpu"` with `config.webgpu_power_preference = "HighPerformance"` (targets NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ada Lovelace `sm_89`).
- **High-Refresh Display**: `config.max_fps = 144` and `config.animation_fps = 120` bypass the default 60 FPS cap.
- **DWM Composition Bypass**: `config.win32_system_backdrop = "Disable"` prevents Windows Desktop Window Manager composition lag.
- **Custom Block Glyphs**: `config.custom_block_glyphs = true` ensures pixel-perfect rendering of half-block ANSI characters (`U+2580..U+259F`) directly in shader memory.
- **Zero Cursor Redraws**: `config.cursor_blink_rate = 0` eliminates periodic timer interrupts when idle.

entries.title: LUA52_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
- **Kitty Keyboard Protocol**: `config.enable_kitty_keyboard = true` distinguishes keydown, keyup, and key-repeat events for real-time controls (WASD, arrows, jump).
- **CSI u Key Encoding**: `config.enable_csi_u_key_encoding = true` handles chorded modifiers without ambiguity.
- **Fullscreen Action**: `F11` and `Alt+Enter` trigger `wezterm.action.ToggleFullScreen`.

---

entries.title: LUA52_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
- **Class and Field Contracts**:
  ```lua
  ---@class Player
  ---@field entity Entity
  ---@field speed number
  ---@field health integer
  local Player = {}
  ```
- **Strict Data Schemas**: Protect item, enemy, and level configuration tables with `(exact)`:
  ```lua
  ---@class (exact) WeaponConfig
  ---@field damage number
  ---@field cooldown number
  ---@field projectile_speed number
  ```
- **Engine Stubs & Meta Definitions**:
  Mark definition files with `---@meta` (`types/bevy.d.lua`) to provide IDE autocompletion for host engine reflection without polluting runtime globals.

entries.title: LUA52_SOVEREIGN_GUIDE.md
entries.text:
- **Linter**: `selene` for AST-level scope analysis and flagging undeclared variables.
- **Formatter**: `stylua` for zero-configuration, deterministic formatting.
- **Debugger**: Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) via `local-lua-debugger-vscode` or `mobdebug`.
- **Hot Reload Architecture**: Decouple state from logic: persist entity variables in Rust ECS components or a dedicated `_STATE` table so reloading script files preserves active game sessions.

---

entries.title: MODERN_WEB_GUIDELINES.md
entries.text:
Every web surface combines the highest aesthetic standards of the three premier design systems: ```mermaid flowchart TD M3["Google Material Design 3
Dynamic Color Tokens & Surface Containers"] --> U["Sovereign UI/UX Pro"] AP["Apple macOS Design
Subtle Vibrancy, Precision Typography & Windows"] --> U FL["Microsoft Fluent 2
Acrylic Depth & Micro-Interactions"] --> U U --> OUT["Sub-100ms Native Web Experience"] ``` 1. **Google Material Design 3 (M3)**: - Dynamic tonal palettes: Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Surface, and Surface Container (`lowest`, `low`, `standard`, `high`, `highest`). - Clear elevation tiers with pure CSS shadow tokens (`--elevation-1` through `--elevation-5`). - Accessible color contrast (minimum 4.5:1 for body copy, 3:1 for large display headers) compliant with WCAG 2.2 AAA. 2. **Apple macOS Interface Rigor**: - Windowing aesthetics: elegant 12px/16px rounded window borders, subtle backdrop filters (`backdrop-filter: blur(20px)`), and titlebars. - Precision typographic hierarchy using system font stacks (`-apple-system`, `BlinkMacSystemFont`, `Inter`, `Roboto`, `system-ui`). - Tabular numerals (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) for all performance metrics, dates, and currency values. 3. **Microsoft Fluent UI 2 Depth**: - Subtle acrylic surface lighting and smooth cubic-bezier transitions (`transition: all 120ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`). - Zero jarring layout jumps; seamless dark and light mode adaptation via CSS custom properties. ---

entries.title: MODERN_WEB_GUIDELINES.md
entries.text:
To eliminate AI-generated mediocrity and maintain sovereign software taste:

- **Strictly Zero Emojis (`ARCH-009`)**:
  - Zero pictographic emoji characters (`\p{Extended_Pictographic}`) in UI labels, buttons, navigation menus, metadata, or documentation.
  - Use vector SVG icons (e.g. Material Design Icons, Lucide) exclusively.
- **Strictly Zero Marketing Puffery (`ARCH-010`)**:
  - Strictly zero empty marketing tropes ("revolutionary", "unleash", "delve", "seamless", "game-changer", or unverified wrapper claims).
  - Every UI claim must be backed by real, deterministic endpoints (`/api/...`, `/ok`).
- **Strictly Zero Unrequested SaaS Decoration**:
  - No decorative purple/neon mesh gradients.
  - No fake user ratings or simulated customer testimonials (`aggregateRating` emitted only with authentic user reviews).
- **Deterministic No-JS Fallback**:
  - When client JavaScript is disabled, the core information architecture remains accessible via semantic HTML5 SSR (`server.ts`).

---

entries.title: MODERN_WEB_GUIDELINES.md
entries.text:
Target performance envelope for all production deployments:

| Metric | Target | Enforced Invariant |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **First Contentful Paint (FCP)** | `< 200 ms` | Server-rendered HTML streamed directly via Bun v1.4.4. |
| **Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)** | `< 1.2 s` | Zero heavy client-side hydrate waterfalls; critical CSS inlined. |
| **Interaction to Next Paint (INP)** | `< 50 ms` | Native DOM event delegation; zero blocking JavaScript loops. |
| **Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)** | `0.00` | Explicit `width` and `height` attributes on all images and canvases. |
| **First Input Delay (FID)** | `< 16 ms` | Sub-frame execution; compute offloaded to Web Workers or WASM. |

---

entries.title: MODERN_WEB_GUIDELINES.md
entries.text:
No UI feature is considered complete until verified through automated browser pipelines:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Dev as Agent / Engineer
    participant Bun as Bun SSR Server
    participant PW as Playwright / Agent-Browser
    participant LH as Lighthouse CI Gate

    Dev->>Bun: Start local server (Bun.serve)
    Dev->>PW: Navigate to route & execute interactions
    PW->>PW: Inspect accessibility tree (browser_a11y_tree)
    PW->>PW: Capture high-res visual screenshot
    Dev->>LH: Run Lighthouse audit (LCP, CLS, INP, A11y)
    LH-->>Dev: Verified 100% Quality Pass
```

entries.title: MODERN_WEB_GUIDELINES.md
entries.text:
- Every route and modal must have an automated test verifying:
  1. Successful HTTP 200 response with correct content-type header.
  2. Document title and meta description presence.
  3. Interactive elements trigger state changes within 50ms.
  4. Responsive viewport behavior (desktop 1920x1080, tablet 768x1024, mobile 375x667).

entries.title: NAMING.md
entries.text:
One multicall binary, like `bun`, `cargo` or `busybox`: `ay <command> [subcommand]`. Package `aphrody`
(crate), binary `ay`. Every former standalone tool becomes a subcommand; no per-tool binaries, no
aliases.

| Command | Replaces | Area |
|---|---|---|
| `ay build [--target <preset>]` | ad hoc cargo/bun invocations | cross-compilation presets (windows-msvc, linux-gnu, linux-musl, macos, wasm32) |
| `ay test` | `just verify-all` pieces | runs cargo, bun and go suites |
| `ay arch check` / `ay arch graph` | `archguard` | architecture gate ARCH-001..017 |
| `ay lock` / `ay doctor` | `xtk lock`, `xtk doctor` | src.lock.json, DEPS, .repo manifest, MAINTAINERS |
| `ay git ...` | `depot` (git shims, slim) | VCS tooling |
| `ay ingest` | `gitingest` | repository digest |
| `ay graph <path>` | `graphify`, `depot-graph` | tree-sitter code graph |
| `ay deploy` | `src-deploy` (Go engine, invoked by `ay`) | deploy |
| `ay bench` | `stack-bench` | benchmarks |
| `ay sys` | (new) | OS, firmware, hardware and software profile |
| `ay ssh exec/cp/hosts/check` | `ssh`, `scp` (OpenSSH client) | pure-Rust SSH (crate `aphrody-remote`, russh): exec on `usa`/`fr1`/`fr2` or `all`, SFTP copy, fleet health |
| `ay web check` | `wck` | web quality gate |
| `ay design` | `gds` | design system |
| `ay forge` | `frg` | forge |
| `ay wl` | `wslg-rs`, `wslg-cosmic-hypr` | Wayland compositor (Linux, Windows, web) |
| `ay scope` | `gamescope-rs` | gamescope mode |
| `ay wsl`, `ay userland` | `unix-distro`, `omarchy-wsl` | WSL distribution, Rust userland |

Bun-based tools (`wck`, `gds`, `frg`) keep their TypeScript implementation; `ay` dispatches to their
AOT-compiled binaries until they are ported.

entries.title: PHILOSOPHY.md
entries.text:
| Principe | Source | Adopté | Rejeté / adapté |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fichiers DEPS par répertoire : `+` autorise, `-` interdit, `!` autorisé mais à retirer (avertissement en presubmit) | `third_party/chromium/src/buildtools/checkdeps/README.md` @ef68a767 [V] | Oui, tel quel : `DEPS.rules` par dossier, mêmes trois préfixes, héritage vers le bas, gate `scripts/checkdeps.ts` | Granularité unité (crate ou package) et pas fichier `#include` : Cargo et bun déclarent déjà les arêtes dans leurs manifestes |
| Les components ne dépendent pas des couches hautes (`//chrome`, `//content/shell`…), peuvent dépendre des basses (`//base`, `//net`, `//mojo`, `//ui`), et entre eux seulement si c'est explicite dans DEPS | `components/README.md` [V] | Oui : couches L0 à L5, dépendance vers le bas libre, latérale libre mais sans cycle, vers le haut interdite sauf `+` explicite | — |
| `//base` : petite bibliothèque commune, code hors src.git ne l'utilise pas ; en Rust, « very small crates, split up by function » | `base/README.md` [V] | Oui : L1 base = crates petites, sans dépendance de domaine | Pas de copie de l'API C++ de base : on prend std + crates.io épinglés |
| gclient DEPS : chaque dépendance externe épinglée par commit de 40 caractères | `DEPS` racine, gate ARCH-014 d'archguard [V] | Oui (DEPS racine existant, `src.lock.json`) | Pas de `hooks` Python arbitraires : les hooks passent par `just` |
| Mojo : interfaces typées (`.mojom`) entre processus/services | `docs/mojo_and_services.md` [V] | L'idée : toute frontière de processus a un schéma versionné (proto pour Lore, JSON Schema/MCP pour l'agent, C ABI versionnée `core_abi_version()`) | Mojo lui-même : trop lié à //base et au sandbox Chromium |
| gn + siso/ninja pour le build | `crates/factory` (F4) | Seulement pour construire Chromium (factory) | Pas de gn pour le reste : cargo et bun suffisent, un second système de build dupliquerait le graphe |

entries.title: PHILOSOPHY.md
entries.text:
1. Une dépendance va vers une couche inférieure ou latérale, jamais vers le haut ; les cycles sont interdits. Contrôlé par `just checkdeps` (CI).
2. Toute exception est écrite dans un `DEPS.rules` avec `!` et un ticket ; elle s'affiche en avertissement jusqu'à sa suppression.
3. Pas de régression, commits bisectables, revue archivée.
4. Une frontière de processus ou de langage a un schéma versionné (C ABI, proto, MCP).
5. Pas d'outil ajouté si bun, cargo ou just le font déjà.

Ces trois crates sont en `publish = false` chez nous, mais `lore` est à renommer avant toute publication, par exemple en `aphrody-lore`. Les noms génériques `cosmic-compat`, `unix-distro` et `smithay-wayland-wire` sont libres aujourd'hui.
- npm : 16 noms libres sur 18. `@aphrody/web` (1.4.7) et `@aphrody/yolo` (3.2.0) existent déjà, publiés par le mainteneur `yohan971`. La page de l'organisation `@aphrody` répond 200, donc le scope est pris. **À confirmer** : `yohan971` est-il le propriétaire ? Si non, le scope `@aphrody` est indisponible et il faut en choisir un autre.

9. Ne jamais commiter `third_party/` ni UnrealEngine dans un dépôt public. Relire `native_nt_gpu.lib`.

entries.text:
- Lore : 12 révisions poussées sur prd, sauvegarde R2.
- Workspace Rust : nightly, cranelift en dev (cold 237→165 s, incrémental 3,05→2,06 s), profil min (2,08 Mo). Tests en llvm.
- Canaux Chrome en Rust (`aphrody x channels`).
- Fabrique fr1 : build labs_agent Stable 157 en cours (69 % à 2 h 22) ; sync ChromiumOS R157 OK (42 Go) ; flags chromite vérifiés dans le source.
- NativeLink 1.8.5 : serveur sur fr1, workers sur prd et fr2, joignables par le mesh. siso envoie bien les actions (vérifié dans les logs des workers).

entries.title: REVIEW-2026-11-12.md
entries.text:
1. **Affirmations non sourcées** : V8 annoncé 15.9.85 alors que c'est 16.0.25, et des docs STACK/shell rédigées de mémoire. Correctif adopté : marquer [V]/[NV]. Beaucoup de [NV] restent dans docs/shell.
2. **Trois sessions sur le même sujet** (shell : brush, niubash, brush) : travail perdu, réglages qui se marchent dessus. Partage décidé ensuite : nt-03 au bas niveau, cette session sur Chromium.
3. **WSL** : build d'une distro lancé, puis interdit. Du temps fr1 perdu ; tout est nettoyé.
4. **Forks en masse** : 210 forks vercel-labs d'un coup, 175 refusés par l'anti-abus GitHub (403). Doublons (-1/-2/-3) entre sessions. Un fork ne sert que s'il est patché ou vendorisé : la plupart ne le sont pas.
5. **Secret** : le token gh a été écrit dans un script /tmp sur fr1 (supprimé à la fin) et passé dans des URL git (visibles dans ps). À éviter : utiliser un credential helper. Le token est à faire tourner, comme les secrets déjà exposés plus tôt.
6. **NativeLink lancé en root au premier déploiement** : n'importe quel pair du mesh pouvait exécuter des commandes en root sur prd et fr2. Corrigé : DynamicUser, ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges. Effet de bord ouvert : les actions échouent en « Permission denied » à l'exécution de clang (bit exécutable ou montage), à corriger avant le premier build distant.
7. **Test distant lancé pendant le build local** : il était en concurrence sur fr1, l'utilisateur l'a arrêté. Les tests REAPI se font quand fr1 est libre, ou depuis prd.
8. **Agent Oils** : livré. OSH 0.38.0 natif Windows (clang-cl/lld), 2,5 Mo, 36/36 smoke, boucle 5,5× plus rapide que brush ; fork() remplacé par exécution in-process + CreateProcessW. Limites : écrivain infini in-process bloque, sortie >16 Mo, pas de job control (docs/shell/oils-windows.md). Transmis à nt-03.
9. **ROADMAP.md (M0–M6 : runtime JS, bundler…)** ne correspond plus à la vision actuelle (labs = Chromium optimisé). Voir la nouvelle section Fabrique.

entries.title: ROOT-ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
Tout nom doit pouvoir changer sans réécrire le code : nom du dépôt (`src`), CLI, binaires, crates, packages npm, scope, site, URL git.
- **Une seule source** : `identity.toml` à la racine (name, cli, scope npm, crate_prefix, domain, git remotes, lore remote). Tout le reste en dérive.
- **Génération** : `ay identity apply` (Rust) réécrit les champs `name`, `[[bin]]`, `package.json#name` et les remotes depuis identity.toml ; `ay identity check` sert de garde en CI (aucun nom en dur ailleurs).
- **Code** : aucun nom de produit en dur. Utiliser `env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME")`/`CARGO_BIN_NAME`, et lire le scope ou le domaine via une crate `identity` générée par build.rs depuis identity.toml.
- **Chemins** : jamais de `C:\src` ni de `/home/ubuntu/...` en dur. Les chemins sont relatifs à la racine du dépôt (détectée par `.lore`/`Cargo.toml`), sinon ils viennent de variables (`SRC_ROOT`, `XDG_*`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%`) via `dirs`.
- **Multiplateforme** : chaque binaire compile et teste sur windows-msvc et linux-gnu. Les scripts .sh/.ps1 sont remplacés par des recettes `just` qui appellent des binaires Rust ou bun (pas de bash ni de pwsh requis).
- **Renommer = une PR** : modifier identity.toml, puis `ay identity apply`, puis `just ci`. Pour les noms déjà publiés (crates.io, npm), ajouter un alias de transition.

entries.title: ROOT-ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
#### 5.1 `aphrody dev`

```
fs watcher (io/notify) --changed paths--> module graph (bundle, incremental)
      |                                         |
      |                       +-----------------+------------------+
      |                       v                 v                  v
      |               server env (RSC)   client env (browser)  edge env
      |                transpile/oxc      transpile + React Refresh
      |                       |                 |
      |                       v                 v
      |              runtime (V8 isolate)   dev HTTP server (net) --HMR WebSocket--> browser
      |               renders Flight + HTML   serves /_next/static/* from memory
      v
tailwind scanner (oxide) --candidates--> tailwind compiler --> css (lightningcss) --> HMR CSS update
```
- One process, with a tokio multi-thread runtime for I/O. JS executes on dedicated isolate threads: one server isolate per environment, plus a worker pool for parallel route rendering.
- Modules are transpiled lazily, on first request, and cached by content hash in `.aphrody/cache` (zstd).
- HMR has two paths: client modules use React Refresh boundaries, and server modules invalidate the Flight payload, which the client refetches with `router.refresh()` semantics.

#### 5.2 `aphrody build`

```
next.config.* (evaluated in runtime) --> route discovery (app/, pages/)
  --> bundle: 3 environments (server-rsc, server-ssr, client) + edge, code splitting
  --> rsc: client-reference manifest, server-action manifest
  --> tailwind + css: one CSS file per layout chunk, minified
  --> prerender: execute static routes in runtime --> HTML + .rsc payloads
  --> deploy: write .vercel/output (Build Output API v3) + .next-compatible manifests
```
- `build` is deterministic: the same inputs and lockfile produce byte-identical output. CI checks this with a two-build hash comparison.
- `build --target <vercel|node|static|oci>` selects the output adapter. The default is `vercel`, which is BOA v3.

#### 5.3 `aphrody serve`

```
.vercel/output/config.json --routes--> router (net, matches BOA v3 route phases)
   |-- static/            served from disk/mmap, immutable cache headers
   |-- functions/*.func   loaded into runtime isolates (pooled), handler per route
   |-- *.prerender-config ISR: stale-while-revalidate with an on-disk cache
```
- `serve` runs the same artifact Vercel would run, so local and remote behavior match. This is also how the Build Output v3 suite runs in CI without network access.

#### 5.4 `aphrody deploy`

```
build --target vercel  -->  .vercel/output
  --> provider = vercel: POST files and the deployment through the Vercel REST API (token from env), same contract as `vercel deploy --prebuilt`
  --> provider = oci:    single static binary + output dir --> OCI image (no Dockerfile needed)
  --> provider = static: static/ only (routes that need functions are rejected at build time)
```
- Credentials are read only from the environment or the OS keychain, never from the repo.

entries.title: ROOT-ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
Next.js-compatible means that an existing project runs unmodified with `aphrody dev` and `aphrody build`. A `next` bin shim lets the upstream Next.js test harness drive it.

What stays JavaScript: React, react-dom and the `next/*` client and server runtime modules come from npm (MIT) and execute in V8. Their behavior is not reimplemented. What becomes Rust is everything Next.js normally does in its Node-side build and server: config loading, route-tree building, bundling (Turbopack/webpack roles), manifests, the server request pipeline, the cache, and static generation.

Components:
1. **Route tree** (`next`). It scans `app/` for `page`, `layout`, `template`, `loading`, `error`, `not-found`, `route`, `default`, parallel `@slot`, intercepting `(..)` and groups `(group)`, and `pages/` for legacy routes. It produces the same route manifests (`app-paths-manifest.json`, `routes-manifest.json`, `prerender-manifest.json`, `middleware-manifest.json`) because the Next.js runtime and the deploy adapter read them.
2. **Environments** (`bundle`). Each environment is a separate rolldown build with its own conditions: `react-server` for RSC, `node`/`edge` for SSR, and `browser` for the client. Directives (`"use client"`, `"use server"`, `"use cache"`) are detected in the oxc AST:
   - `"use client"` modules are replaced in the RSC graph by client-reference stubs (`registerClientReference(id, export)`).
   - `"use server"` functions are replaced in the client graph by `createServerReference(actionId)`. The action id is a stable hash of module path plus export name, salted per build.
3. **Flight** (`rsc`). Rust does not encode Flight. Encoding happens in V8 with React's own `react-server-dom` server build, which keeps the format identical to the upstream React version. Rust supplies three things: (a) the client-reference manifest in the shape that `react-server-dom-webpack` and `react-server-dom-turbopack` expect (`id`, `chunks`, `name`); (b) the module loading shim (`__webpack_require__`/`__turbopack_require__` equivalents) mapped onto aphrody chunks; (c) a streaming bridge that moves Flight chunks from the RSC isolate to the SSR isolate and the HTTP response without copying (`bytes::Bytes` over a channel). The `rsc` crate also includes a Flight decoder for tests and inspection.
4. **Request pipeline** (`next` + `net`): proxy/middleware (edge env), then route match, then RSC render (Flight), then SSR (HTML from Flight, `renderToReadableStream`), then streaming response. Navigation requests that carry an `RSC: 1` header skip SSR. Partial prerendering is supported: the static shell is generated at build time and dynamic holes are filled at request time over the same stream.
5. **Server actions**: a POST with `Next-Action: <id>` is looked up in the server-action manifest, then the arguments are decoded with React's `decodeReply` in V8. Return values and revalidation are serialized as Flight.
6. **Caching**: `fetch` cache, `"use cache"`, `cacheTag`/`cacheLife`, `revalidatePath`/`revalidateTag`. The storage interface is pluggable: memory for `dev`, disk for `serve`, and the provider for `deploy`. The semantics follow the pinned Next.js version, which the e2e suite verifies.
7. **Next.js modules served natively**: `next/image` (optimizer on Rust image codecs, chosen in M4), `next/font` (font fetch and subsetting at build time via fontique/skrifa), `next/og` (rendered by `renderer`).

Version policy: one Next.js minor line at a time, pinned in the conformance lock. The `next` package version in a user project must match that supported line; on a mismatch, `aphrody` warns.

entries.title: ROOT-ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
The goal is byte-identical CSS to `tailwindcss` v4 at the pinned upstream commit, for the same input CSS and sources.

```
input.css --(lightningcss parse)--> AST --(at-rule pass)--> DesignSystem
   @import "tailwindcss" | @theme | @source | @utility | @variant | @custom-variant | @plugin | @config | @apply
sources --(tailwind-oxide scanner)--> candidate strings
candidates --(candidate parser)--> {variants[], utility, value, modifier, important}
   --(DesignSystem.compile)--> rules --(sort: layer, variant order, property order)--> CSS AST
   --(lightningcss: nesting, vendor prefixes, @property, color-mix fallbacks, minify)--> output.css
```

- **Port scope**: `packages/tailwindcss/src` (MIT) is ported module by module: `design-system`, `candidate`, `utilities`, `variants`, `theme`, `compile`, `apply`, `at-import`, `css-functions`, `property-order`, `sort`. Each Rust module records the upstream file and commit it was ported from, which keeps later re-syncs mechanical.
- **Scanner**: upstream `crates/oxide` (package `tailwindcss-oxide`, MIT, edition 2021, verified at commit `b08bf83a`) is used as a git dependency pinned to the conformance commit. If its dependency tree blocks that, it is vendored into `crates/tailwind-oxide` with the upstream MIT license and a NOTICE file. Its tests run unchanged (suite 4).
- **JS plugins and `@config`**: legacy `tailwind.config.js` and `@plugin` modules run in the aphrody runtime through a small plugin API bridge (`addUtilities`, `matchUtilities`, `addVariant`, `theme()`). Pure-CSS configs never start an isolate.
- **Integration points**: the `bundle` CSS pipeline (automatic for `@import "tailwindcss"`), `aphrody tailwind` (CLI-compatible with `@tailwindcss/cli` flags), and a PostCSS-compatible entry for the integration suite.
- **Verification**: the upstream `*.test.ts` files mostly use `toMatchInlineSnapshot` around `compile()` or `run()`. A one-time extractor (in `conformance`) converts each case into a `{input css, candidates, expected css}` fixture at the pinned commit. Rust tests diff against those fixtures (suite 5).

entries.title: ROOT-ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
- **Schema**: the shadcn registry schemas are the compatibility contract: `registry.json` and `registry-item.json`, which exist at `shadcn-ui/ui@dd41d19e:apps/v4/public/schema/`. The `registry` crate models them with serde using `deny_unknown_fields` off and `$schema` preserved, and it validates every document against the upstream JSON Schema in tests.
- **Item types**: `registry:ui`, `registry:component`, `registry:block`, `registry:lib`, `registry:hook`, `registry:page`, `registry:file`, `registry:style`, `registry:theme`, `registry:item`, with `files`, `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, `registryDependencies`, `cssVars`, `css`, `envVars`, `docs`, `meta`.
- **Client**: `aphrody add <item | url | @namespace/item>` reads `components.json` (style, aliases, `tailwind.css`, `iconLibrary`, `registries`). It resolves `registryDependencies` transitively, rewrites import aliases, merges `cssVars`/`css` into the Tailwind v4 CSS entry (`@theme inline`, `:root`, `.dark`), and installs npm dependencies through `pm`. Its observable result must equal `shadcn add` on the same project, which is checked by snapshotting the file tree.
- **Server**: `aphrody registry build` turns a `registry.json` into the static `r/<name>.json` items. The output is servable by `aphrody serve` or any static host.
- **Components**: components ship as TSX source (the shadcn model), not as Rust widgets. The first-party set is built on Base UI primitives (`@base-ui/react` 1.9.0 at `mui/base-ui@5aacdbb7`, MIT), so the Base UI test suite (suite 7) is the behavioral oracle for interaction and accessibility under the aphrody runtime and test runner.

ROOT-ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
- **Project license**: MIT OR Apache-2.0.
- **Allowed dependency licenses**: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Zlib, Unicode-3.0, CC0-1.0, Unlicense, and MPL-2.0 under the rule below.
- **MPL-2.0** (lightningcss, stylo, selectors, cssparser, servo): used unmodified, as registry dependencies only. No MPL file is copied, patched or vendored into this repo. If a fix is needed, it goes upstream and the pin is bumped. A `[patch]` entry against an MPL crate is forbidden.
- **Denied**: GPL, LGPL, AGPL (any version), SSPL, BUSL and other non-OSI licenses, plus any code whose license GitHub reports as NOASSERTION, unless a manual review clears it and the review is recorded here.
- **Study-only**: Bun (`oven-sh/bun`). GitHub reports NOASSERTION (`repos.tsv`). Its `LICENSE.md` at `43850629` says Bun itself is MIT but statically links LGPL-2 JavaScriptCore/WebKit and bundles other C/C++ code, so the tree is mixed. Contributors may read it and describe the ideas, but must not copy, translate line by line or vendor its code. The same applies to Zed/GPUI (NOASSERTION).
- **Test suites as oracles**: upstream suites are fetched at pinned commits into the ignored `conformance/upstream/` and run there. They are not committed, so their licenses (Test262 BSD-style, WPT 3-Clause BSD, Bun NOASSERTION) do not enter the source tree.
- **Enforcement**: `cargo-deny` (`deny.toml`, added in M0) with `licenses`, `bans` (no `openssl-sys`, which keeps the TLS stack on rustls) and `sources` (crates.io, plus `vendor/` path patches) runs before every change is submitted to Lore.

entries.title: ROOT-ARCHITECTURE.md
entries.text:
- **Errors**: `thiserror` in library crates and one `miette`-style diagnostic renderer in `cli`. The choice is made in M1 and pinned then.
- **Concurrency**: tokio for I/O. JS runs on isolate threads, never on tokio worker threads. CPU-heavy work (parse, bundle, scan) goes to rayon-style pools inside rolldown and oxide.
- **Cache**: `.aphrody/cache/<kind>/<blake-or-sha256>`, zstd-compressed and content-addressed, shared by `dev`, `build` and `test`.
- **Telemetry**: none.

entries.title: STACK-ROADMAP.md
entries.text:
**Navigateurs et moteurs (embarquement et agents)**
1. Chromium/Blink, Stable 157 (`third_party/chrome-channels.toml`) : la référence WPT, WebGPU (Dawn) et V8.
2. CEF via cef-rs 156.4.0+156.0.26 : la meilleure façon d'embarquer Blink en Rust, une seule version derrière Stable.
3. `headless_shell` (checkout 160.0.8158.0) : la meilleure base pour un Chromium agent, sans `//chrome` ni UI, avec CDP natif.
4. Lightpanda 1.1.0-dev (Zig, `build.zig.zon`) : la meilleure interface agent (CDP, BiDi, MCP, markdown). Licence AGPL, donc processus séparé obligatoire.
5. Obscura 0.1.0 (Rust, V8 150.4 via deno_core 0.412) : la philosophie la plus proche de labs (MCP, SSRF, stealth), mais très jeune.
6. Electron 43.8.9 (Chromium 150) : compatibilité maximale, mais 7 versions majeures de retard et lourd.
7. Servo 0.8.0 (SpiderMonkey `mozjs_sys` 153.6) : modulaire et en Rust, mais seulement WebDriver, pas de CDP.
8. Blitz 0.3.0-beta.4 : HTML/CSS natif sans JS. Idéal pour l'UI, pas pour le web arbitraire.
9. WebKit/WPE, puis Gecko : le premier n'a pas de cible Windows, le second ne s'embarque pas sur desktop.
10. Helium et Brave : des sources de patchs (debloat, privacy), pas des moteurs à embarquer.
- agent-browser 0.42.0 n'est pas un moteur : c'est la référence UX côté CLI (refs `@e1`, actions vérifiées).

**Moteurs JS**
1. V8 16.0.25 (checkout) / 15.7 (Stable) : performances de référence, via rusty_v8.
2. JavaScriptCore : démarrage rapide (Bun), mais les bindings Rust sont faibles.
3. SpiderMonkey (mozjs) : seulement si on prend la voie Servo.
4. QuickJS-ng / quickjs-jit =0.14.2 (nsh) : le meilleur moteur pour scripter ou sandboxer en Rust.
5. Hermes / Static Hermes : AOT intéressant, mais aucun binding mûr [NV].
6. Boa, puis Nova : Rust pur, mais lents ou encore en recherche.

**Compilateurs et toolchains**
1. clang/LLVM de Chromium : ThinLTO, PGO et orderfile.
2. rustc sur le même LLVM : condition pour la cross-language LTO avec Chromium.
3. rustc Cranelift : uniquement pour la boucle de dev.
4. `zig cc` : cross-compilation C.
5. MSVC : seulement pour le linker et le SDK.
- TypeScript, dans l'ordre : tsgo (type-check) > oxc (parse, transform, minify) > swc > esbuild > tsc.

**Rendu et GPU**
- Raster : Skia Graphite > Vello 0.12 > WebRender. Vello est la voie Rust.
- API GPU : wgpu 30 côté Rust, Dawn côté Blink. Garder `webgpu.h` comme frontière commune.
- Layout : Taffy 0.15, le seul pivot commun à GPUI, nsh, Blitz et Servo.
- Texte : HarfBuzz > Parley (+harfrust/skrifa) > font-kit+swash (GPUI) > cosmic-text.
- Style : stylo, le seul moteur CSS complet en Rust.

**Équivalents C++ → Rust**
- Remplacer par le Rust : ICU → ICU4X 2 ; HarfBuzz → harfrust ; FreeType → skrifa ; zlib → zlib-rs ; libpng → png ; Dawn → wgpu (côté Rust) ; libxml → xml5ever.
- BoringSSL → rustls + aws-lc-rs, mais seulement côté serveur aphrody.
- Pas d'équivalent mûr, on garde le C++ : ANGLE, PDFium, V8.

**Documentation**
1. Tauri et Electron : la doc la plus complète.
2. Dioxus : bon guide, rustdoc et exemples.
3. wgpu, Servo, oxc : doc correcte.
4. Chromium : très vaste, mais éclatée et souvent périmée.
5. Lightpanda et Obscura : README et bancs d'essai seulement.
6. GPUI et gpui-kit : on apprend surtout par les exemples.

entries.text:
**Critique**
1. **Git ou Lore : il faut choisir.** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:11` contredit `.git` ; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` est supprimé, donc il n'y a plus de CI.
   - Correctif : git canonique (miroir `aphrody-labs/labs`), Lore traité comme un simple produit. Restaurer la CI sous forme de `just ci`, puis réécrire la ligne 11.
2. **Écart V8.** `Cargo.toml:196-197` tire V8 15.2 précompilé, alors que `docs/ENGINE-DECISION.md` impose V8 16.0.25.
   - Correctif : retirer les deux lignes ; ajouter `[patch.crates-io] v8 = { path = "vendor/rusty_v8" }` quand le fork existera.
   - Construire V8 une seule fois et le stocker en artefact CAS (`depot-cas`), jamais pendant `cargo build`.
3. **ENGINE-DECISION se contredit** (lignes 59, 98 et 125).
   - Correctif : oracle de conformance = Stable 157 ; embarquement = CEF 156 / Electron 150 ; 160 = uniquement source d'extraction.

**Élevé**
4. **Deux workspaces revendiquent le même produit.** `C:\src\Cargo.toml:6-8` contient `next`, `react`, `ui`, `rt`, `rust-stack`, `aphrody-design-*` ; `labs/crates/cli/Cargo.toml:3` décrit aussi aphrody.
   - Correctif : `src` = outillage souverain uniquement ; tout le code produit va dans labs.
5. **Lore surdimensionne la build.** `Cargo.toml:3` compile tous les crates : aws, hashicorp, fuse, capi, chaos, otlp/tonic, quinn (583 paquets dans le lock).
   - Correctif : sortir Lore dans `vcs/lore/` en workspace séparé, ou au minimum ajouter `default-members`.
6. **Trois copies de Lore** : `crates/lore*`, `tools/lore/`, `vendor/`, plus `src/third_party/vcs/lore`.
   - Correctif : une seule source, `aphrody-labs/lore`, épinglée dans `src.lock.json`.
7. **Le harnais de test est lié au binaire de prod** (`crates/cli/Cargo.toml:21`).
   - Correctif : passer conformance en dev-dependency ou en binaire `labs-conformance` séparé.
8. **Toolchain flottante.** Nightly sans date dans labs ; pas de `rust-toolchain.toml` dans src (MSRV 1.85 contre 1.97).
   - Correctif : `nightly-2026-11-12` identique dans les deux repos, piloté par `src.lock.json`.
9. **Politique de versions.** Tout est en `=x.y.z`, y compris des pré-versions (`Cargo.toml:41-197`).
   - Correctif : plages caret, avec Cargo.lock comme seul pin. `=` seulement pour les couples liés et commentés (gpui-pre, blitz/stylo, bitcode).
10. **Orgs mélangées.** `C:\src\DEPS:22-40` mêle `aphrody-dev` et `aphrody-labs`, avec des entrées qui pointent vers le repo lui-même.
    - Correctif : `aphrody-labs` comme seule org de forks ; supprimer les auto-références.

**Moyen**
11. **Builds non portables et lents.**
    - `target-cpu=native` (`src/tools.toml:450-483`) : passer à `x86-64-v3`.
    - lld-link désactivé (`labs/.cargo/config.toml:33-36`) + `lto=fat` + 1 CGU (`Cargo.toml:287-290`) : profil `release` en thin LTO / 16 CGU, et `dist` en fat LTO réservé à la CI.
12. **Rustflags.** Ils sont dupliqués dans `.cargo/config.toml:1-36`, et `+crt-static` est incompatible avec les DLL CEF.
    - Correctif : regrouper dans `[build]` seul ; pas de crt-static sur les cibles qui embarquent CEF.
13. **Un clone frais ne compile pas** : `vendor/`, `licenses/`, `third_party/` ne sont pas suivis.
    - Correctif : les versionner, ou les remplacer par des dépendances git épinglées.
14. **Docs dans `C:\src\docs`** : 35 fichiers, quatre docs d'architecture concurrentes, des versions Bun dans les noms de fichiers.
    - Correctif : un seul `ARCHITECTURE.md`, le reste dans `docs/history/`, et `AGENTS.md` comme unique fichier d'instructions agent.
15. **Scripts `.sh` dupliqués avec `ay`.**
    - Correctif : sous-commandes `ay vendor` et `ay channels`, plus un `labs/justfile`.

**Doublons et goulots de l'écosystème**
- **winit** en trois versions : `=0.31.0-beta.3` (dioxus), `=0.31.0-beta.4` (blitz), 0.30.2 (anyrender). Aligner sur beta.4 via `[patch]`.
- **wgpu** en trois versions : 29 (nsh), 30.0.1 (dioxus/blitz), git `cddb2f5` (gpui-fast/Zed). Pour éviter deux wgpu dans un même binaire, garder GPUI et Blitz dans des binaires séparés.

entries.text:
**(a) Web full-stack, façon Vercel en self-hosted**
0. **Socle** : `cargo new`, nightly daté, workspace avec `resolver = "3"`, `cargo-binstall dioxus-cli` (même version que dioxus).
1. **Framework** : `dioxus = { version = "0.7.10", features = ["fullstack","router"] }` (stable). Prévoir la bascule vers 0.8 dès la sortie stable ; 0.8.0-alpha.3 est seulement à tester en branche.
2. **UI** : `rsx!`, dioxus-signals et stores, dioxus-router.
3. **Serveur** : axum 0.8.9, tower 0.5.2, tower-http 0.6.8, hyper 1.8, tokio 1.52.
   - Rendu par dioxus-ssr et dioxus-server ; hydratation via dioxus-web et interpreter-js.
4. **Server functions** : `#[server]` (dioxus-fullstack), transport HTTP ou websocket. Base de données : sqlx ou sea-orm.
5. **WASM** : wasm-bindgen 0.2.127, wasm-split (code splitting), `wasm-opt` via `dx bundle`.
6. **WebGPU web** : wgpu 30 avec le backend `webgpu`, dans un composant canvas isolé. Dioxus n'offre rien de prêt pour ça, c'est à construire.
7. **Styles et composants** :
   - CSS : Tailwind v4 (CLI standalone, sans Node) branché sur `asset!()` de manganis ;
   - primitives : dioxus-components (git, aucune release, le Base UI de Dioxus) ;
   - registre de composants façon shadcn : à créer, `aphrody-ui`.
8. **Interop JS** (React, Svelte, Vue, Solid) : à faire via des îlots web-components. Pas d'interop native.
9. **Outillage** : hot-patch avec subsecond, dioxus-devtools, tests avec dioxus-test (expérimental), Playwright pour l'e2e.
10. **Plateforme aphrody** (à construire, `aphrody-*`) :
    - builder de déploiements immuables (tâche CAS) ;
    - previews par PR, promotion, rollback ;
    - routeur edge sur axum + rustls (TLS/ACME via `instant-acme`) ;
    - ISR avec revalidation par tags ;
    - optimisation d'images à la volée (crate `image`) ;
    - KV et Blob, observabilité OpenTelemetry, feature flags, firewall.

**(b) Desktop natif**, dans l'ordre de priorité
1. **Blitz natif** (`dioxus` feature `native`, blitz 0.3.0-beta.4, stylo rev `2dca345`, html5ever 0.40.1, taffy 0.15, parley 0.13, anyrender 0.14 / vello 0.12, wgpu 30, `winit =0.31.0-beta.4`, accesskit 0.25).
   - Le même RSX que le web, en CSS réel, sans JS.
2. **GPUI** (gpui-kit 0.9.1, avec gpui-pre =0.3.12 ou la feature `gpui-fast` 0.1.14) : pour les apps de type éditeur ou trading, avec environ 60 composants de style shadcn.
   - Binaire séparé à cause du wgpu git.
3. **Tauri v3** (3.0.0-alpha.6) avec wry : pour réutiliser la stack TS, Tailwind et shadcn. Utiliser cef-rs 156 quand il faut un Blink uniforme.
4. **Electron 43.8.9** : uniquement pour la compatibilité Node. À éviter par défaut.

Pour l'ordre d'exécution : web fullstack (étapes 1 à 7), puis Blitz natif (même code), puis plateforme aphrody, puis GPUI pour la console ops, puis Tauri/CEF.

```
    agent-cdp/          # client CDP + BiDi, token, garde SSRF (philosophie Obscura)
```

**Ce qu'on garde, supprime, ajoute**

- **On supprime ou on déplace** :

entries.title: TOOLCHAIN_UPSTREAM_LEVERS.md
entries.text:
Ordered by expected gain per unit of effort for this repo:

1. **D10 + W1**: Defender exclusions plus a Dev Drive for `build-dir`, ccache and ThinLTO caches. Helps cargo, Bun and Chromium at once.
2. **C3/C4**: short `build.build-dir` path. The new per-unit layout adds one `-L` per dependency, and with sccache as wrapper this is the most likely cause of `os error 206`.
3. **C6**: `-Zfeature-unification` with `resolver.feature-unification = "workspace"`, so `-p` builds stop rebuilding shared dependencies.
4. **R13**: `rust-lld` as the windows-msvc linker for dev and test binaries.
5. **R5/C2**: Cranelift for workspace members in dev (LLVM for dependencies), excluding crates whose tests need unwinding.
6. **R8**: an internal `lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 16`, `incremental = true` profile next to the fat-LTO dist profile. Post-LTO modules get reused.
7. **R1**: `-Zthreads=4..8` for dev and check builds, validated with `cargo build --timings` (C8) and `-Zself-profile` (R11).
8. **B5/P1**: ThinLTO cache plus `-gcodeview-ghash` in the Bun fork's Windows link. Also check B10 (is JSC being built locally?).
9. **B3**: install ccache for Bun's C/C++ (picked up automatically). Use `--lto=off --rust-lto=off --rust-codegen-units=16 --rust-incremental=on` for release iteration (B6).
10. **C5**: checksum freshness in the Linux containers, where Docker Desktop bind mounts make mtimes unreliable. For Chromium, iterate in `out/Default`, not `out/Release`, and use `--no-history` for fresh checkouts (D2, D8).

Already on, no action: `-Zembed-metadata=no` on nightly (C1), share-generics in dev (R4), rust-lld on x86_64 Linux GNU (R12/G2). No effect, remove or document: `split-debuginfo = "unpacked"` on Windows (R15), `/DEBUG:FASTLINK` in lld (L3), `enable_nacl` (D9).

entries.title: TOOLCHAIN_UPSTREAM_LEVERS.md
entries.text:
rustc, cargo, LLVM, gcc, glibc and depot_tools need no patches: every lever above is a configuration change. The two patches below are in the Bun fork, where the build flags are hard-coded and have no environment hook.

1. **P1: ThinLTO cache and precomputed type hashes in the Bun Windows link** (`third_party/bun/scripts/build/flags.ts`, the release entry at `1167-1200` and the `/Z7` entry at `342-347`).
   - Add `/lldltocache:<cacheDir>/thinlto` and `/lldltocachepolicy:cache_size=10%:cache_size_bytes=40g:cache_size_files=100000`, copied from Chromium's policy (`chromium/src/build/config/compiler/BUILD.gn:788-800`).
   - Add `--thinlto-cache-dir` for the ELF lane.
   - Add `-gcodeview-ghash` next to `/Z7`.
   - Why a patch: `flags.ts` takes no extra linker flags from the environment, and lld only caches when the flag is passed (`lld/COFF/LTO.cpp:212-213`).
   - Gate: local builds only (not `cfg.ci`), the same rule the fork already uses for `-Zthreads`, so release artifacts stay byte-reproducible.
2. **P2 (optional): a `release-fast` build profile** in `third_party/bun/scripts/build/profiles.ts` (next to `release-local`, `139-144`).
   - Settings: `lto: false, rustLto: false, rustCodegenUnits: 16, rustIncremental: true`.
   - Mirror `rustCodegenUnits` and `rustIncremental` to `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_*` (`scripts/build/rust.ts:663-670`).
   - Also add `[profile.dev.package."*"] debug = "line-tables-only"` to the fork's `Cargo.toml`.
   - Why a patch: the four flags in B6 work today, but there is no way to make them one named profile or apply them to dev.
   - Low priority: carry it only if the long flag line becomes a habit.

Rejected as patches:

- sccache support in the Bun ninja graph (B2): it depends on wrappers forwarding rustc's JSON artifact notifications.
- Blobless clones in gclient (D4): high maintenance, and `--no-history` covers most of the benefit.
- Swapping the host linker for Bun build scripts (B9): small gain, and the fork documents why it chose `link.exe`.

entries.title: UNIX.md
entries.text:
1. **Aether-in-Rust Theme Compiler (`themes.rs`)**:
   - Parses upstream Omarchy `colors.toml` palettes from `C:\src\third_party\omarchy\themes\*\colors.toml` and embeds all 23 canonical Omarchy themes plus 2 sovereign presets (`aphrody-m3-dark`, `cachyos-emerald`) for standalone zero-dependency execution.
   - Compiles any `ColorsToml` simultaneously into 6 target formats:
     1. `hyprland-colors.conf` (`col.active_border`, `col.inactive_border`, shadow, `groupbar`)
     2. `cosmic-theme.ron` (COSMIC Desktop RON theme)
     3. `bar.css` (Waybar / Quickshell CSS)
     4. `terminal.toml` (Alacritty / Rio / Ghostty TOML)
     5. `aether-theme.lua` (Neovim `omacom/aether.nvim` Lua spec)
     6. `theme.css` (CSS Custom Properties for Web/TUI preview)
2. **Plugin & Marketplace Engine (`plugins.rs`)**:
   - Catalogs all 16 built-in Omarchy shell plugins (`agents`, `background`, `bar`, `clipboard`, `dev-gallery`, `dock`, `emojis`, `image-picker`, `lock`, `menu`, `notifications`, `osd`, `panels`, `polkit`, `reminders`, `services`).
   - Streams `C:\src\third_party\omarchy-plugin-marketplace\registry.json` (6,443 community sources) with sub-second filtering and scaffolds new Quickshell plugins (`manifest.json` + QML entry point).
3. **Arch GitLab + CachyOS + Omarchy Package & Patch Engine (`packages.rs`)**:
   - Synthesizes unified repository manifests across `[cachyos-v3]`, `[cachyos-core-v3]`, `[cachyos-extra-v3]`, `[omarchy]`, and Arch `[core]`/`[extra]`/`[multilib]`.
   - Verifies and emits the Linux `7.4` kernel patch series (`0001-bore-cachy.patch`, `0001-prjc-cachy.patch`, `dkms-clang.patch`, `nvidia/0005-Fix-build-on-Linux-7.4.patch`, `0001-aufs-7.4-merge-v20260914.patch`, `0001-acpi-call.patch`) alongside the WSL2 `/dev/dxg` + `hv_sock` + `virtio_fs` + `/dev/ntsync` kconfig fragment.
4. **Native WSL2 Distro Builder & Launcher (`wsl.rs`)**:
   - Emits `.wslconfig` (`memory=24GB`, `processors=24`, `networkingMode=mirrored`, `dnsTunneling=true`, `autoProxy=true`, `guiApplications=true`, custom `bzImage-7.4-cachyos-omarchy`), `rootfs/etc/wsl.conf` (`systemd=true`), `rootfs/etc/wsl-distribution.conf` (`oobe` command `/usr/lib/wsl/first-setup-aphrody-omarchy.sh`, default user `aphrody`), `zram-generator.conf`, Hyper-V `getty@.service` unit masks, and reproducible `build-aphrody-omarchy-wsl.sh`.
   - Orchestrates `wsl.exe --install --from-file` / `wsl.exe --import` with automatic dry-run safety and live `wsl --list` inspection.

---

```
C:\src\crates\wayland\
├── Cargo.toml                      # Rust 2024 workspace
└── crates\
    ├── dx12-winui-core\            # D3D12 Ultimate device, GPU fences, NT shared textures, DirectComposition & WinUI DispatcherQueue
    ├── smithay-wayland-wire\       # Pure-Rust Wayland binary wire protocol, AF_HYPERV (hv_sock) transport, DMA-BUF & Fractional Scale globals
    ├── hypr-tiler\                 # Hyprland Dwindle BSP, Master-Stack, WindowRuleV2, 120Hz spring physics, Omarchy keybinds & /dev/dxg damage coalescer
    ├── cosmic-compat\              # COSMIC layer-shell, workspaces, Material 3 & Omarchy Aether RON theme bridge, HiDPI zero-blur protocol descriptors
```

entries.title: WAYLAND.md
entries.text:
1. **Direct3D 12 Ultimate & Zero-Copy `/dev/dxg` Bridge (`dx12-winui-core` + `hypr-tiler::omarchy`)**:
   - Targets NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (`0x10DE:0x2786`, Ada Lovelace `sm_89`, 12 GB VRAM, Feature Level `12_2`).
   - Allocates and imports cross-VM NT shared GPU textures (`DXGI_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM`) paired with `DxgDmaBufDamageTracker`, coalescing Wayland surface damage regions into minimal bounding scissor rects for zero-copy `/dev/dxg` DMA-BUF presentation.
2. **Omarchy Keyboard-First Tiling Model (`hypr-tiler`)**:
   - Built-in `OmarchyKeybindRegistry` modeling Omarchy chords:
     - `Super+Space`: Omarchy root launcher (`omarchy-menu`)
     - `Super+K`: Keybinding HUD (`omarchy-menu-keybindings`)
     - `Super+Return`: GPU terminal (`ghostty`)
     - `Super+W`: Close active window
     - `Super+1..9` / `Super+Shift+1..9`: Direct workspace focus and window movement
     - `Super+Shift+T`: Live Aether theme hot-switch (`omarchy-wsl themes export <theme>`)
3. **COSMIC Theme Bridge & Zero-Blur HiDPI Scaling (`cosmic-compat` + `smithay-wayland-wire`)**:
   - `CosmicTheme::from_omarchy_palette(...)` maps Omarchy Aether palettes directly into COSMIC Desktop `.ron` theme structures.
   - Advertises 10 Wayland globals including `ext_workspace_manager_v1`, `zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1` (v4), `wp_fractional_scale_manager_v1` (v1), and `wp_viewporter` (v1).
   - `WslgHiDpiScalingDescriptor` computes exact 120ths fractional scale factors from Windows 11 monitor DPI (e.g., 144 DPI = `180/120` = 1.5x, mapping `2560x1440` logical coordinates cleanly onto `3840x2160` physical buffers without Weston/XWayland bilinear blur).

---

entries.text:
| Host | Default Rust target | Linker | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows 11 | `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` | MSVC `link.exe` or `rust-lld` | The only Windows target used for first-party code. |
| Windows, MinGW ABI needed | `x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm` | LLVM (`lld`, `libunwind`), no GCC | Use instead of `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`, which pulls in a MinGW-w64 GCC toolchain. Not installed by default. |
| Linux | `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` / `-musl` | system `cc` / static musl | musl is the container target (`Dockerfile` builder stage). |
| Linux -> Windows | `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` | `cargo xwin` | Downloads the MSVC CRT and Windows SDK; no Wine, no MinGW. |
| Any -> Linux/macOS | various | `cargo zigbuild` | Zig as the C linker for cross builds. |

`cargo-xwin` and `cargo-zigbuild` are installed in `~/.cargo/bin`. Cross-compilation presets belong in
`src build --target` (see `docs/CONSOLIDATION_PLAN.md`), not in ad hoc scripts.

entries.title: WINDOWS_UNIX_TOOLCHAIN.md
entries.text:
Git for Windows ships an MSYS2 runtime (`/usr/bin` in Git Bash). First-party tooling must not depend
on it. The replacements are native Rust binaries:

| MSYS2 / GNU tool | Rust replacement | Status on this machine |
|---|---|---|
| coreutils (`ls`, `cp`, `sort`, ...) | uutils `coreutils` multicall, built with `--features windows` | 0.12.0 via winget (`WinGet/Links/ls.exe`) |
| findutils (`find`, `xargs`, `locate`) | uutils `findutils` | 0.11.0 in `~/.cargo/bin` |
| diffutils | uutils `diffutils` | installed via winget |
| bash | `brush` (bash-compatible shell) | 0.4.0 in `~/.cargo/bin` |
| grep | `ripgrep` | installed; call it by full path from Bun (see memory note on `rg.cmd`) |

Install and audit these from one manifest with `unix-distro userland status|install`
(`crates/unix`). The `justfile` uses `sh` on Unix and `pwsh` on Windows, so no recipe needs Git Bash.

entries.title: WINDOWS_UNIX_TOOLCHAIN.md
entries.text:
`crates/unix` generates an Arch Linux based WSL2 distribution (CachyOS kernel patches from
`third_party/kernel-patches/<series>/`, Omarchy themes from `third_party/omarchy/themes/`).
Generated configuration follows the documented keys only:

- `.wslconfig` `[wsl2]`: `networkingMode` (`nat`, `mirrored`, ...), `dnsTunneling`, `autoProxy`,
  `firewall`, `memory`, `processors`, `kernel`, `guiApplications`. Path values need escaped backslashes.
  Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/wsl-config
- Mirrored networking needs Windows 11 22H2 or later and gives IPv6, `127.0.0.1` to Windows services,
  and multicast. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/networking
- Distribution packaging (`wsl --install --from-file`, `/etc/wsl-distribution.conf`):
  https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/build-custom-distro

Memory and processor counts are derived from the probed host or passed as flags; nothing is hardcoded
to one machine.

entries.title: WINDOWS_UNIX_TOOLCHAIN.md
entries.text:
Goal: the same Wayland compositor and protocol stack runs natively on Linux, on Windows 11 and in the
browser (wasm32), with no regression against upstream behaviour. Today WSLg runs Weston in the Linux
guest plus an RDP channel; Linux GPU access goes through `/dev/dxg` and Mesa's d3d12 driver
(https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/tutorials/gpu-compute).

What ties Wayland to Unix, and the replacement for each:

| Unix dependency | Where | Windows replacement | Web replacement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AF_UNIX` stream socket | libwayland, `wayland-backend`, smithay `src/wayland/socket.rs` | Windows `AF_UNIX` (stream only) or named pipes | `WebSocket` / `MessagePort` |
| fd passing (`SCM_RIGHTS`) for `wl_shm` pools, dmabuf, keymaps, data transfer | protocol args of type `fd` | Handle passing: sender `DuplicateHandle`s into the peer and sends the value | Transferable `ArrayBuffer` / `SharedArrayBuffer` |
| `mmap` of shm pools | `wl_shm` | `CreateFileMapping` / `MapViewOfFile` | wasm memory views |
| epoll/calloop event loop | smithay, calloop | IOCP (mio already supports it) | browser event loop |
| drm/gbm/egl/libinput backends | smithay `backend_*` | wgpu (DX12) renderer + winit input | wgpu (WebGPU) renderer + winit web input |
| XWayland | `src/xwayland` | out of scope until the core passes conformance | out of scope |

The fd/handle difference stays inside the transport layer, so the object model, protocol
dispatch and compositor logic are shared across all three platforms. One renderer (wgpu: DX12 on
Windows, Vulkan on Linux, WebGPU in the browser) replaces the GLES/pixman pair.

Clients inside a WSL guest cannot hand fds or handles to the Windows host. They connect over Hyper-V
sockets, and their shm buffers are copied over the stream. Microsoft describes these sockets as
"Data stream only" and "No block memory", so this is the slow path, not zero-copy. The Linux guest is
addressed with the VSOCK template GUID `00000000-facb-11e6-bd58-64006a7986d3`, where the first field
is the port
(https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/make-integration-service).

**No regression, proven by tests:**

- **Baseline:** wlcs (Canonical's Wayland Conformance Test Suite) runs against smithay's `anvil` on
  Linux, using `third_party/smithay/compile_wlcs.sh` and `wlcs_anvil/`.
- **Linux port:** wlcs runs against the ported compositor on Linux. It must match the baseline pass list.
- **Windows and web:** the same protocol scenarios are replayed over the Windows and web transports
  through a wlcs-equivalent harness. wlcs itself loads compositors as Linux shared objects, so it
  cannot run there directly.
- **Every platform:** protocol XML from wayland and wayland-protocols drives code generation, so the
  object model never diverges between platforms.

Order of work:

1. Transport trait with Unix, Windows and web implementations, plus handle-passing tests.
2. Platform-independent object model on top of it.
3. wgpu renderer.
4. winit input and output.
5. wlcs parity on Linux.
6. Windows and web parity harness.

The existing first-party pieces (layout engine, wire codec, D3D12/DXGI host code) live in
`crates/hypr-tiler`, `crates/smithay-wayland-wire`, `crates/dx12-winui-core`, `crates/cosmic-compat`
and `crates/wslg-cli` and will be folded into this design.

entries.title: agents\WINDOWS-NATIVE-PORT.md
entries.text: Les deux upstreams supportent déjà Windows natif : named pipes pour les IPC (Hermes `\\.\pipe\hermes-gateway-<hash>`), ConPTY et verrous gardés par `sys.platform` ou `process.platform`, lint `windows-footgun` côté Hermes. Les écarts restants viennent du choix du shell et de quelques sondes `/bin/sh`.

entries.title: agents\WINDOWS-NATIVE-PORT.md
entries.text:
| Échec Windows | Patch | Statut |
|---|---|---|
| Shell : `pm.shell.bash()` impose le bash staged de Git for Windows (MSYS). Aucun moyen d'imposer un autre bash | `HERMES_BASH` passe avant le bash staged ; candidat niubash ajouté (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Niubash\winuxcmd\bin\bash.exe`) | OK, `bash()` renvoie niubash |
| Cron `.sh` : `shutil.which("bash")` peut tomber sur le stub WSL de System32 | passe par `pm.shell.bash()` | OK, script cron exécuté par bash 5.3.20 (niubash) |
| Client élevé : `client_elevated` refuse de lancer le gateway depuis une session admin (agents, CI) | opt-in `HERMES_ALLOW_ELEVATED_GATEWAY=1`, à utiliser avec un `HERMES_HOME` dédié | OK |
| `uv sync --all-extras` : l'extra `silk` (pilk) échoue à la compilation native | non patché ; build natif lourd, à faire sur prd | ouvert |
| Course sur l'installation paresseuse des dépendances (`anthropic` : « another Hermes process is installing ») | non patché ; contournement : `hermes pm install` ou `uv pip install anthropic` | ouvert |
| Test `test_run_job_no_agent_uses_configured_interpreter` en échec, déjà présent sur upstream | aucun | ouvert (upstream) |
| AF_UNIX absent de CPython 3.14 sous Windows | déjà géré upstream (named pipe) | OK |
| fcntl, killpg, pty | déjà gardés upstream (branches POSIX, msvcrt et ConPTY) | OK |

Vérification e2e (HERMES_HOME isolé, HERMES_BASH=niubash) : outil terminal (fichier écrit), mémoire écrite puis relue dans une nouvelle session, skill `port-check` créée par `skill_manage`, job cron `--script tick.sh --no-agent` lancé avec `cron run` : succès.

entries.title: agents\WINDOWS-NATIVE-PORT.md
entries.text:
| Échec Windows | Patch | Statut |
|---|---|---|
| L'outil exec impose PowerShell (`getShellConfig`), alors que la machine interdit pwsh | `OPENCLAW_EXEC_SHELL=bash` sélectionne un bash natif ; `OPENCLAW_BASH` force son chemin (niubash) ; `detectRuntimeShell` annonce `bash` | OK, tests unitaires (41/41 sous Windows) |
| meeting-bot : les sondes `command -v` passent par `/bin/sh -lc`, donc toute commande est vue absente | `where.exe /q` sous win32 (runtime-setup, configured-node-host) | OK, 362 tests meeting-bot passent |
| `bun install` réécrit package.json (workspaces/overrides depuis pnpm-workspace.yaml) et résout d'autres versions que pnpm-lock, d'où l'échec de tsdown (`getDefaultSocketTimeout` manquant dans @aws-sdk/core) | non patché ; le build source se fait avec pnpm (CI) ; sur le PC, la release npm s'installe avec `bun add openclaw` | ouvert (bun vs lockfile pnpm) |
| launchd et systemd (`/bin/sh` dans launchd-*.ts, hosted-stop-executor) | aucun ; code propre à macOS et Linux | sans objet |
| Sockets `.sock` (exec-approvals, mac-control) | aucun ; propres à macOS, Windows passe par le gateway WebSocket | sans objet |
| Symlinks : seulement dans des test-support, avec junction sous Windows | aucun | OK |

Vérification e2e (release 2026.11.3 via bun, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR isolé) : `onboard --non-interactive`. La clé API non scopée exige `models.providers.anthropic.headers.anthropic-workspace-id`, ce qui relève de la configuration et non de Windows. `agent --local` : exec puis écriture de MEMORY.md, relu dans une nouvelle session (VALUE=ok). `gateway run`, puis `cron add --every` et `cron run` : le fichier est écrit par l'agent planifié.

1. Render oracle: chrome-headless-shell (Stable as the reference, Canary as the early-warning signal). It passed 12/12, 6/6 on B, 9/9 on Turnstile and 45/45 features, Lighthouse works, the cold start is about 140 ms and RSS is about 620 MB.
2. Second oracle for cross-engine diffs: Firefox Nightly over BiDi (12/12, B 6/6, 44/45 features). It costs about 1.1 GB and a 2 s cold start. WebKit through Playwright covers JSC/WebKit (B 6/6, 45/45 features).
3. Agent browser, lightweight tier: Lightpanda. It reads all 12/12 sites and passes B 6/6 at about 70 MB and 0.5 CPU-s, starts in 44 ms and loads in 388 ms, and works with both Puppeteer and Playwright. It has no layout, paint, iframes or Turnstile, so it is limited to DOM, JS and RSC work.
4. Agent browser, full-fidelity tier: chs-stable driven directly by Puppeteer or Playwright. agent-browser adds 30 to 90 ms per command and about 400 ms of cold start for no capability gain. It is worth keeping only as an LLM-facing CLI.
5. Obscura is promising (142 MB, 42 ms cold start, Turnstile correct), but the client-navigation click bug and the slower loads (1.4 s median) keep it out of the default path for now.
6. Servo is not ready as an oracle or an agent: 6/12 sites, 36/45 features, WebDriver-only. It is fine for B and D, at about 280 to 380 MB.
7. Embedding (VPS targets): Electron 43 is the most efficient Chromium-based option (12/12, 581 MB, the best LCP). CEF 156 works but needs Xvfb and cannot open new CDP targets, so tooling (Lighthouse, Playwright) breaks. Plan for CDP on the existing page only.
8. Brave and Helium bring nothing for headless use. Brave doubles RSS (about 1.1 GB). Helium is slow and unstable here.
9. Server runtime: Node 24 and Bun serve the Next 16 app with identical client-side results. `next start` booted faster on Node in a single cold sample, so keep Node as the reference and Bun as an option.
10. This changes the ENGINE-DECISION.md paper verdict: chrome-headless-shell becomes the oracle, Lightpanda the cheap agent tier and Firefox Nightly the second opinion. Servo and Obscura stay on a watchlist and should be re-run with this harness (`bun bench.ts --engines servo,obscura`).

entries.title: bun\AOT-LTO-FFI-2026.md
entries.text:
| Mode | Contenu | JIT | Cross-compile | Statut | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bun build --compile` | JS bundlé + runtime | oui | oui, `--target=bun-{linux,windows,darwin}-{x64,arm64}[-musl]` | stable | `docs/compiler/index.mdx`, `executables.mdx` [V] |
| `--compile --bytecode` | bytecode JSC embarqué ; ESM exige `--compile` ; `--bytecode-depth=N` | oui | oui | stable | `docs/compiler/bytecode.mdx` [V] |
| `--bytecode-order` / `BUN_BYTECODE_ORDER_OUT` | ordre du bytecode pour le démarrage | oui | — | depuis #43811 (2026-09-24) | log git [V] |
| `bun compile` (= `build --compile --aot`) | code machine, typecheck tsc, plus de JIT, `--trim`, `--explain` | **non** | **non** (plateforme hôte seulement) | expérimental | `docs/compiler/aot.mdx`, `index.mdx` [V] |
| `--disallow-code-generation-from-strings` | `eval`/`new Function` lèvent une erreur | — | — | #44819 | `executables.mdx:439` [V] |
| `--hardened=on` (build de bun) | stack protector, `_FORTIFY_SOURCE`, clash protection | — | — | #46317 | log git [V] |

Limites de l'AOT (PR #45631, 2026-10-27) [V] :
- Linux ≥ 6.7 : `prctl(PR_SET_MDWE)` interdit toute nouvelle mémoire exécutable. `dlopen()`, appels `bun:ffi` et jusqu'à 256 `JSCallback` ouverts fonctionnent. `cc()` (TinyCC) et les addons qui génèrent du code machine **ne fonctionnent pas**.
- Addons N-API embarquables (`require("./addon.node")`, dossier avec lib voisine via `--aot`) (`executables.mdx:920`) [V].
- Pas de breakpoints. Builds plus longs, sans cache.
- Support Windows de `bun compile` : aucune mention dans la doc ni dans la PR [NV].
- Mesures publiées : Linux x64 seulement, sur un build LTO (PR #45631) [V].
